label: 1000 Genomes
quote: The 1000 Genomes Project set out to provide a comprehensive description of common human genetic variation by applying whole-genome sequencing to a diverse set of individuals from multiple populations.
note: Reference panel of 2,504 individuals from 26 populations sequenced to catalogue human genetic variation; participants were sampled by population, not for any exposure or disease.

label: AddNeuroMed Cohort
quote: The primary goal of AddNeuroMed has been to assess longitudinal MRI changes in AD, MCI, and healthy controls using image-acquisition protocols compatible with those used in ADNI [17].
note: Multicentre biomarker study enrolling people with Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment alongside healthy controls; a disease cohort with no exposure component.

label: Adenoma Prevention with Celecoxib trial
quote: The Adenoma Prevention with Celecoxib Trial examined the efficacy and safety of the cyclooxygenase (Cox)-2 inhibitor, celecoxib, for sporadic colorectal adenoma prevention in patients at high risk for colorectal cancer.
note: Randomised trial of celecoxib in patients with prior sporadic colorectal adenomas at high risk of recurrence and colorectal cancer; the intervention is a medication, so there is no environmental exposure.

label: Advanced Study of Aortic Pathology
quote: Briefly, the ASAP cohort is a single-centre, observational cohort study of consecutive patients with aortic valve and/or ascending aortic disease undergoing elective open-heart surgery at the Cardiothoracic Surgery Unit, Karolinska University Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden.
note: Consecutive surgical patients with aortic valve disease and/or ascending aortic dilatation or aneurysm at Karolinska; a patient series with no exposure component.

label: Africa Wits-INDEPTH partnership for Genomics studies
quote: Population-based longitudinal cohort, involving four sub-Saharan African countries representing rural and urban settings: West Africa [Nanoro (Burkina Faso) and Navrongo (Ghana)]; East Africa [Nairobi (Kenya)]; and South Africa (Agincourt, Dikgale/DIMAMO and Soweto).
note: Population-based adult cohort whose stated purpose is cardiometabolic disease and its genomic, environmental and behavioural risk factors, so a population study of one disease family; 'environmental' here means sociodemographic and lifestyle variables collected by questionnaire (a pesticide-exposure item among many), not an exposure-centred design.

label: Arthritis Research UK Osteoarthritis Genetics
quote: Arthritis Research UK Osteoarthritis Genetics (arcOGEN) is a collection of 7410 unrelated, UK-based individuals of European ancestry with knee and/or hip osteoarthritis from the arcOGEN Consortium (Zeggini et al., 2012).
note: Case collection of people with severe knee and/or hip osteoarthritis (with unrelated controls) for genome-wide association; a disease cohort with no exposure component.

label: Asian Cancer Project
quote: In the present analysis, we attempted to replicate these associations using the BCAC component of COGS, comprising 53 835 female breast cancer cases and 50 156 controls (Table 1).
note: Thai breast cancer case-control study contributing cases and controls to the BCAC/COGS analysis (its Table 1 lists the contributing studies; the same paper says the ACP study is funded by the Breast Cancer Research Trust, UK); the cached text has no sentence describing ACP's own recruitment directly.

label: Aspirin for Asymptomatic Atherosclerosis Study
quote: involving 28,980 men and women aged 50 to 75 years living in central Scotland, free of clinical cardiovascular disease, recruited from a community health registry, and had an ABI screening test. Of those, 3350 with a low ABI (< or = 0.95) were entered into the trial, which was powered to detect a 25% proportional risk reduction in events.
note: General-population screening trial: people free of clinical cardiovascular disease were entered only if they had a low ankle brachial index, a marker of asymptomatic atherosclerosis and higher cardiovascular risk, so the trial cohort is selected for disease risk; aspirin is a medication, not an environmental exposure.

label: AtheroExpress
quote: A data linkage study was performed using patients from the Athero-Express biobank study who underwent CEA in two Dutch tertiary referral hospitals between 2002 and 2020.
note: Biobank of patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy and other vascular surgery for atherosclerotic disease, with plaque tissue and follow-up for cardiovascular events; a patient cohort with no exposure component.

label: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study
quote: In each of four US communities--Forsyth County, North Carolina, Jackson, Mississippi, suburbs of Minneapolis, Minnesota, and Washington County, Maryland--4,000 adults aged 45-64 years will be examined twice, three years apart.
note: Community-based general population cohort set up to study atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease, like Framingham; exposures are measured only as risk factors among many variables.

label: Atopic Dermatitis Research Network
quote: The goal is to understand more about the immune system of AD patients which may lead to new therapeutic targets that minimize the likelihood of cutaneous infections that frequently exacerbate this disease.
note: Consortium of clinical centres running registry and clinical studies in patients with atopic dermatitis (with non-atopic controls); infection is an outcome studied, not the basis of recruitment, so there is no exposure component.

label: Australia Cancer Study
quote: Additional case women missed at the major treatment centers were identified through cancer registries and, with the treating doctor’s permission, invited to participate (recruitment through the New South Wales and Victorian Cancer Registries was conducted in parallel under a separately funded study: the Australian Cancer Study).
note: Registry-based recruitment of women newly diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer (the ovarian-cancer arm of the Australian Cancer Study) alongside population controls for the Australian case-control analyses; a disease cohort with no exposure component.

label: Australian Ovarian Cancer Study
quote: The second study was a national population-based case-control study of ovarian cancer, the AOCS.
note: National population-based case-control study of women with newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian cancer and population controls; a disease cohort with no exposure component.

label: Australian Twin Registry
quote: The Australian Twin Registry (ATR) is a national volunteer resource of twin pairs and higher-order multiples willing to consider participating in health, medical, and scientific research.
note: Volunteer twin registry supporting research across many fields; twins are enrolled for their twin status, not for an exposure or a disease.

label: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children
quote: The Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC) is a transgenerational prospective observational study investigating influences on health and development across the life course.
note: General birth cohort of pregnancies in the Bristol area followed for health and development; it is listed in the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue and records many environmental exposures, but these sit among genetic, epigenetic, psychological and social ones under a broad stated purpose rather than an exposure-centred design, so exposure is no.

label: Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster trials
quote: Between 1981 and 2000, 6609 children (<18 years of age) were treated in five consecutive trials of the Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster (BFM) study group for childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
note: Aggregation of successive treatment trials enrolling children and adolescents with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; a patient cohort with no exposure component.

label: Bladder Cancer Prognosis Programme
quote: The BCPP is a prospective longitudinal cohort study of all patients with newly diagnosed bladder cancer within the West Midlands (UK), investigating the influence of lifestyle factors on recurrence and progression, health-related quality of life, the predictive effect of a panel of molecular markers on recurrence or progression, and the establishment of Europe's largest comprehensive bladder cancer bio-repository.
note: Prospective cohort of all newly diagnosed bladder cancer patients in the West Midlands; lifestyle factors are one of several aims within a disease-defined cohort, not the basis of recruitment nor its main subject, so exposure is no.

label: Brazilian Cohort
quote: The sample comprised 45 babies (26 males aged mean ± SD 25.50 ± 7.17 months; 19 females aged mean ± SD 24.79 ± 6.73 months), 44 with confirmed Zika-associated congenital microcephaly and one baby with familial congenital microcephaly.
note: Presented as a population reference exome set, but the 45 babies were recruited as suspected microcephaly cases during the 2015–2016 Zika outbreak in Rio Grande do Norte, 44 with confirmed Zika-associated congenital microcephaly; they are defined by the disease, not by exposure to the virus.

label: Breast Cancer Association Consortium
quote: We pooled tumor marker and epidemiological risk factor data from 35,568 invasive breast cancer case patients from 34 studies participating in the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.
note: Consortium pooling breast cancer case-control and cohort studies; classified by what it collects, breast cancer patients and their controls.

label: Bruneck study
quote: The study was launched in summer 1990 when a sex- and age-stratified random sample of all inhabitants of Bruneck (n=1,000) was invited to participate in the study.
note: Random population sample of Bruneck residents set up to study atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease, the same design as ARIC or Framingham; its focus has since broadened to other age-related diseases, hence medium confidence.

label: Cancer and Leukemia Group B
quote: In the ensuing 50 years, the Cancer and Leukemia Group B has expanded to national and even international membership, and its research programs have expanded to include all of the common adult solid tumors and hematologic malignancies in a multidisciplinary effort to improve the outcomes for patients with cancer and to better understand the biology of malignant disease.
note: Cooperative group running treatment trials in patients with adult solid tumours and haematological malignancies; classified by what it collects, cancer patients.

label: Cancer Genome Atlas
quote: TCGA is a collaboration between the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) that has generated comprehensive, multi-dimensional maps of the key genomic changes in 33 types of cancer.
note: Programme of tumour and matched-normal specimens from patients with 33 cancer types, genomically characterised; a tumour bank collecting cancer patients, with no exposure component.

label: Cancer Prevention Study
quote: The Cancer Prevention Study II (CPS-II), which began in 1982, is a prospective mortality study of approximately 1.2 million American men and women.
note: American Cancer Society general-population mortality cohort whose subject is cancer and its risk factors, so a population study of one disease family; its baseline questionnaire covers occupational exposures, diet, alcohol and tobacco among many other items, but the source states no exposure-centred design purpose, so exposure is no (the diet-focused CPS-II Nutrition Cohort is a separate sub-cohort term).

label: Cancer Prostate in Sweden
quote: The population-based, case–control study in Sweden, named Cancer Prostate in Sweden (CAPS) was used to complete fine-mapping in the study.18 Cases with pathologically diagnosed PCa were recruited from regional cancer registries in Sweden, between July 2001 and October 2003.
note: Population-based case-control study of men with newly diagnosed prostate cancer recruited from Swedish regional cancer registries, with matched controls; a disease cohort with no exposure component.

label: Candesartan in Heart failure Assessment of Reduction in Mortality and morbidity
quote: CHARM is intended to randomize 6,500 patients with symptomatic heart failure from 26 countries in Europe, the United States, Canada, South Africa, and Australia.
note: Programme of three placebo-controlled trials of candesartan in patients with symptomatic heart failure; classified by what it collects, heart failure patients; candesartan is a medication, not an environmental exposure.

label: Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network
quote: CAGE participants were recruited in a population-based or hospital-based setting, depending on the design of member studies.
note: A network of Japanese, Vietnamese and Sri Lankan population- and hospital-based member studies whose stated purpose is cardiometabolic traits and disorders, so it is a population study of that disease family; environmental factors are mentioned only in passing, not as a design purpose.

label: Cardiogenics Study
quote: This initiative recruited 918 participants (459 patients with myocardial infarction and 459 normal controls) in five centres: Cambridge (UK), Leicester (UK), Lübeck (Germany), Regensburg (Germany), and Paris (France).
note: A case-control collection of myocardial infarction patients and controls assembled for coronary artery disease genetics; recruitment is by disease, not by any environmental exposure.

label: CARDIoGRAMplusC4D
quote: Cases were selected for inclusion following the standard criteria for CAD and myocardial infarction used in the CARDIoGRAM study (details for the stage 2 and 3 cohorts are given in Supplementary Table 2).
note: A consortium pooling coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction case-control studies, so it collects patients with that disease; no exposure enters its design.

label: Carolina Head and Neck Cancer Epidemiology
quote: A population-based case-control study of incident SCCHN, the Carolina Head and Neck Cancer Study was carried out in 2002-2006 in 46 counties in North Carolina.
note: A population-based case-control study of incident head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, so its cases are patients; tobacco and alcohol are studied as risk factors but do not define the cohort.

label: CARTaGENE cohort (CHU Sainte-Justine, Quebec, Canada)
quote: In population-based cohorts, participants are not recruited for a particular disease but represent a random selection among the population, minimizing the need to correct for bias in measured phenotypes.
note: Quebec's population-based biobank of adults aged 40-69 recruited as a random selection of the population for chronic disease in general; neither a disease nor an exposure defines it.

label: Center for Autism Research and Treatment
note: A university autism research and clinical centre through which participants with a confirmed ASD diagnosis are recruited (alongside typically developing controls), so it is a patient collection for autism; it is a centre rather than a defined study, hence medium confidence. No environmental exposure is involved.

label: Center on Antisocial Drug Dependence
quote: This study includes individuals from two cohorts within CADD: the longitudinal twin sample (LTS) and the community twin sample (CTS) (Rhea et al., 2013).
note: A Colorado centre whose community-based twin samples are studied for the etiology of substance use disorders and related externalising conditions; addiction counts as a disease and it is the centre's stated purpose, so a population study of disease. Substance use is studied as the disorder, not as an environmental exposure defining the sample.

label: Centre dEtude du Polymorphisme Humain
quote: The CEPH collection includes families collected by R. White (Utah), J. Dausset (French), J. Gusella (Venezuelan), and J. Egeland (Amish).
note: A foundation whose collection is reference families (Utah, French, Venezuelan, Amish) used for mapping human genetic variation; the families are not selected for a disease or an exposure, and the foundation's interest in complex diseases is a broad mission, not a cohort design.

label: Chicago Asthma Genetics
quote: Participants were recruited through the adult and pediatric asthma clinics at the University of Chicago Medical Center as part of the Chicago Asthma Genetics study.
note: Adults and children with clinically confirmed asthma recruited through asthma clinics for asthma genetics; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Children, Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm, Epidemiology
exposures: exposure at home and day care | furred animal and mite allergens | temperature, indoor humidity, air change rate and NO2
quote: Inclusion in the study was made at 3-4 months of age. At that time, and before induction of allergic disease/ asthma of the child, a questionnaire focused on exposure, genetics and socio-economic factors was answered. Settled dust was sampled for later analysis of furred animal and mite allergens.
note: A Stockholm population-based birth cohort (Milieu in its name) designed to find risk factors for childhood asthma and allergy, with baseline exposure questionnaires, home dust sampling for allergens and home measurements of NO2, humidity and air change; so a population study of asthma and allergic disease whose design centres on environmental exposures.

label: Cholesterol and Atherosclerosis Pharmacogenetics
quote: The Cholesterol and Pharmacogenetics (CAP) trial involved 944 healthy volunteers, 609 of whom were Caucasian, treated for six weeks with simvastatin 40 mg/day at two study sites (University of California, Los Angeles and San Francisco General Hospital) [5].
note: Healthy volunteers given six weeks of simvastatin in a pharmacogenetics trial of lipid response; a medication is not an environmental exposure and the participants have no disease.

label: Cilento study
quote: The discovery sample includes 1600 volunteer individuals recruited through a population-based sampling strategy in three small isolated villages of the Cilento region, South Italy (Campora, Gioi and Cardile).
note: A population-based sample of residents of three genetically isolated Cilento villages used for genetics of complex traits and diseases in general; the EGA project's focus on cardiovascular traits is one use of the cohort, not its recruitment basis, so neither disease nor exposure defines it.

label: COIN
quote: The COIN trial aims to determine the best way of treating patients whose bowel cancer has spread.
note: A phase III trial cohort of patients with advanced colorectal cancer comparing continuous and intermittent chemotherapy; chemotherapy is a treatment, not an exposure.

label: COIN-B
quote: We enrolled patients with advanced colorectal cancer who had received no previous chemotherapy for metastases.
note: A randomised phase 2 trial cohort of patients with advanced colorectal cancer testing intermittent versus continuous cetuximab; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Colorectal Cancer Study of Austria
quote: A total of 3,264 participants was genotyped including 142 CRC cases, 492 high-risk polyps, 837 low-risk polyps, and 1,793 polyp-free controls verified by colonoscopy.
note: An Austrian case-control collection of colorectal cancer and polyp cases with colonoscopy-verified polyp-free controls for colorectal neoplasia genetics; diet and smoking are questionnaire covariates, not the recruitment basis.

label: Consortium for the Longitudinal Evaluation of African Americans with Early Rheumatoid Arthritis
quote: The CLEAR Registry is a National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases-funded program which enrolls self-defined African Americans with RA as defined by the revised American Rheumatism Association (now the American College of Rheumatology [ACR]) criteria.
note: A registry of African Americans with rheumatoid arthritis combining a longitudinal early-RA cohort and a cross-sectional cohort; a patient registry, with environmental factors studied only as correlates of severity.

label: Consortium of Minority Population Genome-Wide Association Studies of Stroke
quote: Using METAL, we conducted meta-analyses of GWAS in 14 746 African Americans (1365 ischemic and 1592 total stroke cases) from COMPASS, and tested genetic variants with P<10(-6) for validation in METASTROKE, a consortium of ischemic stroke genetic studies in European-ancestry populations.
note: A consortium pooling stroke cases and controls from minority-population cohorts and case-control studies to find stroke susceptibility loci; it collects a disease, not an exposure.

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg
quote: KORA (Cooperative Health Research in the Region Augsburg) is a regional research platform for population-based surveys and subsequent follow-up studies in the fields of epidemiology, health economics, and health care research.
note: A population-based research platform of Augsburg surveys and follow-ups (with an MI registry as one component) covering diabetes, cardiovascular disease, ageing, allergy and health services; its purpose is broad and the environment is one topic among many, not a design purpose.

label: Copenhagen Hospital Biobank
quote: The Copenhagen Hospital Biobank (CHB) 23 was established in the Capital Region of Denmark and contains leftover ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid whole blood samples from patients undergoing red cell typing or antibody screening.
note: A biobank of leftover blood samples from hospital patients of every kind in the Capital Region of Denmark; the patients are not selected for any one disease and no exposure is involved.

label: CROATIA-Korcula Study
quote: It examines a family-based, cross-sectional genetics population cohort of adult volunteers recruited in the island of Korčula, Croatia between 2007 and 2014.
note: A population isolate cohort of adult volunteers on Korcula island recruited to find genes for common diseases in general (heart disease, diabetes, glaucoma, stroke); a broad purpose, so not a disease cohort, and no exposure basis.

label: Danish Glostrup Cohort
quote: The 1936-cohort is a population-based prospective age-specific cohort that consists of 1198 Danish subjects born in 1936, who were resident in municipalities nearby Glostrup Hospital (Denmark) in 1976.
note: A population-based cohort of people born in 1936 living near Glostrup Hospital, examined at age 60; the atherosclerosis analysis in the COHO definition is one use of a general population survey rather than a recruitment basis, so neither disease nor exposure defines it.

label: Diabetes Genetics in Pakistan
quote: Participants in the investigation (Table 1) were from two studies of South Asian individuals; the United Kingdom Asian Diabetes Study (UKADS; 857 participants with type 2 diabetes, 417 without) [2], [3] and the Diabetes Genetics in Pakistan study (DGP; 821 participants with type 2 diabetes, 1167 without) [3].
note: A Pakistani case-control collection of people with type 2 diabetes and normoglycaemic controls for diabetes genetics; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Diabetes in Mexico Study
quote: Supplementary Methods Study participants Diabetes in Mexico Study (DMS): Individuals were enrolled in the study, recruited from two tertiary level institutions (IMSS and ISSSTE) located in Mexico City.
note: A Mexico City collection of type 2 diabetes cases and non-diabetic controls recruited at two tertiary institutions for the SIGMA diabetes GWAS; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Diabetes Prevention Program
quote: The Diabetes Prevention Program is a randomized clinical trial testing strategies to prevent or delay the development of type 2 diabetes in high-risk individuals with elevated fasting plasma glucose concentrations and impaired glucose tolerance.
note: A trial cohort of people with impaired glucose tolerance and raised fasting glucose, selected for high risk of type 2 diabetes; the lifestyle and metformin arms are interventions, not exposures.

label: Diabetes Reduction Assessment with Ramipril and Rosiglitazone Medication
quote: People with impaired fasting glucose or impaired glucose tolerance were randomised to ramipril (15 mg/day) or placebo and rosiglitazone (8 mg/day) or placebo with a 2x2 factorial design.
note: A trial cohort of people with impaired fasting glucose or impaired glucose tolerance randomised to ramipril and rosiglitazone to prevent diabetes; a pre-disease (at-risk) cohort, and the drugs are treatments, not exposures.

label: Diabetes Research on Patient Stratification
note: IMI DIRECT combines prospective cohorts of prediabetic people (an at-risk group) and patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes for biomarker discovery; no environmental exposure defines it.

label: Dortmund Health Study
quote: We included cross-sectional data of five population-based longitudinal cohort studies from different areas of Germany: the Dortmund Health Study (DHS) conducted in the city of Dortmund
note: A population-based sample of Dortmund residents whose stated aim is the prevalence and incidence of headache types, with other chronic conditions and social factors as secondary aims; medium because the aim also names other chronic conditions.

label: Duke Cognition Cohort
note: A US cohort of adults (ages 18-77) with cognitive testing and genotypes, contributed to COGENT's meta-analysis of general cognitive function in healthy individuals; cognition is a trait, and no source in the bundle or cache describes an exposure or disease basis.

label: DUNDEE
note: The Dundee collection site of the Scottish high-grade serous ovarian cancer whole-genome sequencing study: a patient series with matched tumour and blood samples.

label: Durban Diabetes Study
quote: Population-based cross-sectional survey using multistage cluster sampling of adults aged ≥18 years in Durban (eThekwini municipality), KwaZulu-Natal
note: A population-based cross-sectional survey of urban Black residents of Durban whose primary research focus is diabetes, with other chronic diseases secondary; no exposure defines it.

label: Dutch and Belgian Lung Cancer Screening Trial
exposures: smoking exposure (years smoked, cigarettes/day, years quit)
quote: Inviting current and former smokers (quit <or= 10 years ago) who smoked >15 cigarettes/day during >25 years or >10 cigarettes/day during >30 years was most optimal.
note: The NELSON trial selected heavy current and former smokers from the Dutch and Belgian general population for CT lung-cancer screening: recruited as smokers, and at high risk of lung cancer.

label: Dutch Microbiome Project
quote: The goal of the Dutch Microbiome Project is to investigate the interactions between microbiome, host, environment and human health.
note: Gut-microbiome profiling of participants of the general-population Lifelines cohort; environment is one of several factors studied, not a design purpose, and no disease selects the participants.

label: Edinburgh Stroke Study
note: A prospective hospital series of patients with recent stroke in Edinburgh, followed for outcome; no environmental exposure is involved.

label: ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48
note: A randomised anticoagulation trial whose participants all have atrial fibrillation; the drug comparison is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: EPIGEN
quote: A population-based genome-wide analysis of 6,487 individuals was performed in the context of worldwide genomic diversity to elucidate how ancestry, kinship, and inbreeding interact in three populations with different histories from the Northeast (African ancestry: 50%), Southeast, and South (both with European ancestry >70%) of Brazil.
note: An aggregation of three population-based Brazilian cohorts (the 1982 Pelotas birth cohort, the Bambui ageing cohort and Salvador-SCAALA) used for population genomics and the genetic epidemiology of complex diseases in general; neither exposure nor a single disease defines it.

label: Erasmus Rucphen Family Study
quote: A family-based cohort study that is embedded in the Genetic Research in Isolated Populations (GRIP) program in the South West of the Netherlands.
note: A family-based cohort of descendants of founder families in a genetically isolated Dutch population, assembled for genetic research on complex disorders in general; selection is by genealogy, not by exposure or disease.

label: Estonian Biobank
quote: The Estonian Biobank cohort is a volunteer-based sample of the Estonian resident adult population (aged ≥18 years).
note: A volunteer-based population biobank of Estonian adults linked to national registries; a general population resource with no exposure or disease selection.

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer
exposures: nutrition | diet | lifestyle
quote: The European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) is an ongoing multi-centre prospective cohort study designed to investigate the relationship between nutrition and cancer, with the potential for studying other diseases as well.
note: EPIC is a multi-centre general-population cohort designed to study the relationship between nutrition and cancer: a diet-exposure cohort and a population study of cancer.

label: European Prospective Investigation of Cancer-Norfolk
exposures: diet | lifestyle | nutrition
quote: The EPIC-Norfolk study (https://www.epic-norfolk.org.uk) is a population-based prospective cohort study, nested within the European Prospective Investigation of Cancer (EPIC) study, which had the primary aim of exploring the connections between cancer, diet and lifestyle.
note: The Norfolk component of EPIC: a population-based cohort whose primary aim is the connections between cancer, diet and lifestyle, so it inherits EPIC's diet-exposure and cancer verdicts; its own website states the aim of gathering lifestyle and nutritional information.

label: EuroTARGET project
note: A collaborative collection of patients with metastatic renal cell cancer for biomarkers of response to targeted therapy; the therapy is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Extremely Low Gestational Age Newborns
quote: We enrolled 1506 ELGANs born before 28 weeks gestation at 14 sites; 1201 (80%) survived to 2 years corrected age.
note: A birth cohort of infants born before 28 weeks selected for their high risk of brain damage and neurodevelopmental disorders; the exposures it studies (placental microorganisms, inflammation, obstetric antecedents) are perinatal rather than environmental agents, and its later membership of ECHO is not documented in the bundle.

label: Fatty Acid Sensor Study
exposures: omega-3 fatty acid supplementation (fish oil)
quote: A total of 208 participants of the Fatty Acid Sensor (FAS) Study received 5 g fish oil/d, containing 1.9-2.2 g eicosapentaenoic acid and 1.1 g docosahexanoic acid, for 6 wk.
note: A nutrigenomics study of healthy Quebec volunteers given a six-week fish-oil supplement to study gene-diet interaction in the triglyceride response; diet is its main subject (medium, since a supplementation intervention is a borderline environmental exposure), and participants were required to be free of metabolic disease.

label: Finnish Twin Cohort Study
quote: In 2002 and 2006, review papers have described the Finnish Twin Cohort and studies conducted on these population-based, longitudinal data sets with extensive follow-up data.
note: A population-based twin registry aggregation (older cohort, FinnTwin12, FinnTwin16) for health and disease in general; one sub-study of heavy smokers exists, but the aggregation is a twin registry, which is out of scope on both counts.

label: FINRISK
quote: The FINRISK studies were cross‐sectional population surveys carried out in Finland in a systematic and standardized fashion every 5 years since 1972
note: Five-yearly Finnish population surveys monitoring risk factors and non-communicable disease broadly; a general population resource. The cohort profile (PMID:29165699) has no cached text, so the broad purpose rests on the definition and the population-survey description.

label: Flemish Gut Flora Project
quote: The Flemish Gut Flora Project (FGFP) is a population-based cohort that comprises individuals from the Flanders region of Belgium.
note: A population-based microbiome cohort of Flemish volunteers studied in relation to health and lifestyle in general; no exposure or disease defines it.

label: Gabriel Advanced Survey
exposures: exposure to farming environments | specific exposures to cows, straw, and farm milk
quote: The GABRIEL Advanced Surveys (GABRIELA) were conducted to determine factors in farming environments which are fundamental to protecting against asthma and atopic disease.
note: A population-based survey of rural schoolchildren designed to determine which farm-environment exposures protect against asthma and atopic disease: both an exposure cohort and a population study of asthma and allergy.

label: GCAT Genomes for Life
quote: designed to recruit the general population of the north-east region of Spain, Catalonia
note: A general-population prospective cohort of Catalan adults for chronic diseases broadly; neither an exposure nor a single disease defines it.

label: GENESIS
quote: The novelty of the GENESIS (GENE SISters) study is the recruitment of a study population enriched in susceptibility factors by case selection based on familial criteria, with consideration of environmental factors.
note: A French case-control resource of BRCA1/2-negative breast cancer patients with an affected sister, plus unaffected sisters and controls; environmental factors are covariates, not the recruitment basis.

label: Genetic Analysis of Multiple Sclerosis
note: A multinational case-control collection of multiple sclerosis cases with Swedish and UK controls for susceptibility genetics; no environmental exposure is involved.

label: Genetic Consortium for Anorexia Nervosa
note: A consortium pooling DNA samples of anorexia nervosa patients (with matched controls) for GWAS; a case collection for one psychiatric disorder, with no exposure basis.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica
note: Family-based study of Costa Rican children with asthma and their parents, assembled to find genetic determinants of asthma; the participants are asthma patients and no environmental exposure defines the cohort.

label: Genetic Overlap between Metabolic and Psychiatric traits
note: Greek cases-only collection of patients with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes or both, analysed against controls from other cohorts; a patient collection with no exposure basis.

label: Genetic Prostate cancer risk stratification for targeted screening
note: Men aged 40-69 with a family history of prostate cancer recruited for targeted screening with genetic risk profiling and biopsy; selected for prostate cancer risk, not for any exposure.

label: Genetic Research in Isolated
note: Programme of family- and population-based studies of a genetic isolate in the south-west Netherlands (the ERF pedigree) with a broad remit across neuropsychiatric, cardiovascular and metabolic disorders; a general isolate population, not selected by one disease or by any exposure.

label: Genetics of diabetes Audit and Research
note: Tayside cohort of people with type 2 diabetes plus non-diabetic controls linked to health records for diabetes genetics and treatment response; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Genetics of Healthy Aging
note: Nonagenarian sibling pairs and younger controls recruited across Europe to find genes of healthy ageing and longevity; longevity is a trait and ageing is not a disease, and no exposure defines the cohort.

label: GenomeAsia 100K project
note: Population reference sequencing project across Asian population groups, extended by people recruited from South Asian healthcare systems and isolates; a general population resource with no single disease or exposure basis.

label: German Multiple Myeloma Study Group
note: German study group running phase II and III trials for patients at all stages of multiple myeloma; an aggregation of myeloma trial cohorts, so a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Ghana Prostate Study
note: Case-control study of prostate cancer in Accra combining screen-detected and hospital cases with population controls; a disease case-control collection, with obesity and other risk factors measured but no environmental exposure defining it.

label: Glaucoma Inheritance Study in Tasmania
note: Glaucoma patients in Tasmania and their relatives, recruited through diagnosed probands to study familial primary open angle glaucoma; a patient (and at-risk relative) cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Greece Hellenic Isolated Cohorts
note: Umbrella for the MANOLIS and Pomak isolated-population cohorts in Greece, studying the genetics of complex traits; general founder populations with no disease or exposure basis.

label: Health and Retirement Study
note: Nationally representative survey of Americans over 50 on health, cognition, economics and retirement in ageing; a general population cohort with no disease or exposure basis.

label: Health2000 Study
note: National health examination survey of Finnish adults sampled in 2000-2001 to characterise public-health problems broadly; a general population cohort with no disease or exposure basis.

label: Heart Protection Study
note: Randomised trial of simvastatin and antioxidant vitamins in UK adults selected for elevated risk of coronary heart disease death, most already having coronary or other occlusive arterial disease or diabetes; selected for disease risk, and the only exposures are the trial treatments.

label: Hoorn Diabetes Care System
note: Prospective cohort of people with type 2 diabetes in Dutch primary care followed annually for the course of the disease and its complications; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Hospital Discharge Register Sweden
note: Nationwide register of all inpatient discharges in Sweden recording every somatic and psychiatric diagnosis; it is a general administrative patient register covering all diseases, not a cohort of one disease, and no exposure defines it.

label: Human Genetics Initiative
note: NIMH repository collecting the disorder-specific psychiatric genetics collections (bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, depression and others) as patient and control samples; an aggregation of mental-disorder patient collections with no exposure basis.

label: Hunter Community Study
note: Community cohort of adults aged 55-85 randomly sampled from the Newcastle electoral roll to study health and ageing; a general population cohort with no disease or exposure basis.

label: Icelandic Cancer Registry
note: Nationwide registry of all cancer diagnoses in Iceland since 1954; a disease registry of cancer patients with no exposure basis.

label: Identification of Men with a genetic predisposition to ProstAte Cancer
note: International screening study of BRCA1/2 mutation carriers and non-carrier controls from mutation families, followed with annual PSA testing for prostate cancer; selected for genetic prostate cancer risk, with no environmental exposure basis.

label: IIBDGC genotyped CD study
note: Genotyped Crohn's disease (and other IBD) patients collected through the International IBD Genetics Consortium; smoking status was an analysed variable in a gene-smoking interaction study, not the basis of selection, so this is a disease cohort and not an exposure cohort.

label: Indiana Sisters Study
note: Healthy premenopausal sisters recruited in Indiana to study the genetics of bone mineral density; healthy volunteers studied for a trait, with no disease or exposure basis.

label: INfancia y Medio Ambiente Project
exposure categories: air pollution | water | diet | chemical | metal
exposures: environmental pollutants in the air, water and diet during the pregnancy and beginning of life | hormonal disruptors | organochlorine compounds | metals | air pollution | water pollution | arsenic
quote: INMA – INfancia y Medio Ambiente [Environment and Childhood] Project is a research network of several Spanish groups that created a project with the aim to study the paper of the more relevant environmental pollutants in the air, water and diet during the pregnancy and beginning of life, and their effects in the growth and development.
note: Network of Spanish birth cohorts of pregnant women from the general population and their children, built to study prenatal and early-life environmental pollutants (air, water, diet, hormonal disruptors, organochlorines, metals, arsenic) and child growth and development; an exposure-designed birth cohort with no disease basis.

label: International Cancer Genome Consortium-Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
note: Spanish ICGC project sequencing tumour and normal genomes of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia; a patient/tumour cohort with no exposure basis.

label: International Headache Genetics Consortium
note: Consortium pooling migraine cases and controls from headache clinics and population cohorts for migraine GWAS; an aggregation collected for one disease, with no exposure basis.

label: International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium
note: A consortium of multiple sclerosis case collections compared with common controls; it collects patients with one disease and has no exposure design.

label: International Schizophrenia Consortium
note: A consortium of schizophrenia case-control collections; the cases are patients with schizophrenia and nothing in the design concerns environmental exposure.

label: Italian Network on Genetic Isolates Studies
quote: We characterised whole-genome sequences from isolated populations localised in three different geographical areas of Italy
note: A network of genetically isolated population cohorts studied for the genetic basis of complex diseases and traits in general; neither an exposure nor a single-disease design.

label: Leeds Melanoma Cohort
quote: 2183 patients were recruited to the Leeds Melanoma Cohort (LMC) between 2000 and 2012.
note: A cohort of population-ascertained patients with newly diagnosed primary melanoma followed for survival; smoking and vitamin D are analysed as predictors within it, but the participants were selected for the disease, not for an exposure.

label: Leiden Longevity Study
quote: Our study includes families with at least two long-living siblings (men aged 89 years or above; women aged 91 years or above).
note: Families selected for exceptional longevity of sibling pairs, with their offspring and spouses; longevity is a trait, not a disease, and no exposure defines the sample.

label: LifeLines
quote: The LifeLines Cohort Study is a large population-based cohort study and biobank that was established as a resource for research on complex interactions between environmental, phenotypic and genomic factors in the development of chronic diseases and healthy ageing.
note: A three-generation population cohort and biobank of the northern Netherlands with a broad purpose (chronic diseases and healthy ageing); environmental factors are one of many variables, not a stated exposure design.

label: Living Biobank
quote: The Singapore Living Biobank is a collection of healthy population-based Chinese and Malay individuals, for the purpose of phenotype recall study of high-impact variant carriers.
note: A biobank of healthy population-based participants drawn from two Singapore cohorts for recall-by-genotype studies; the only selection is genetic, so neither verdict applies.

label: Los Angeles component of The Womens Contraceptive and Reproductive Experiences Study
note: The Los Angeles cases and controls of a population-based case-control study of breast cancer; the risk factors examined (contraceptive and reproductive history) are medications and reproductive events, not environmental exposures.

label: Lothian Birth Cohorts
quote: All five cohorts comprise non-clinical samples of relatively healthy people from middle to older adulthood with detailed, though not identical, cognitive phenotypes.
note: Two birth cohorts of relatively healthy older people recruited by year of birth and childhood intelligence testing to study cognitive ageing; ageing and normal cognitive variation are not a disease, and no exposure defines them.

label: Lund Stroke Register
note: A population-based register of patients with first-ever stroke in the Lund-Orup district; a disease registry with no exposure design.

label: Marseille Thrombosis Association Study
note: A series of patients with documented venous thrombosis recruited at a thrombophilia centre for genetic study; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Mexican Biobank
quote: To fill this gap, the Mexican Biobank project genotyped 6,057 individuals from 898 rural and urban localities across all 32 states in Mexico at a resolution of 1.8 million genome-wide markers with linked complex trait and disease information creating a valuable nationwide genotype-phenotype database.
note: A nationwide population biobank drawn from a national health survey, with many traits and diseases; a general population resource, not an exposure or disease cohort.

label: MIRAGE
note: A family-based study enrolling Alzheimer disease cases with their unaffected siblings as controls; a patient collection (with related controls) and no exposure design.

label: Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia Collaboration
note: A collaboration of schizophrenia case-control collections of European and African-American ancestry; it collects patients with one disorder and has no exposure basis.

label: MOnica Risk, Genetics, Archiving and Monograph
note: A project pooling prospective European population cohorts surveyed for cardiovascular risk factors and followed for stroke and coronary events; the population cohorts share one disease family as their purpose, and no exposure defines them.

label: Monitoring of Trends and Determinants in Cardiovascular Disease
note: The WHO MONICA Project, standardised surveillance of defined populations in 26 countries with the stated objective of cardiovascular mortality and morbidity; a population study of one disease family with no exposure design.

label: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
note: A population-based sample of adults free of clinical cardiovascular disease at enrolment, set up to study subclinical cardiovascular disease and its progression; the separate MESA Air ancillary study on air pollution is not this cohort's design.

label: Multicenter Family Study
note: Seven collections of multiplex families ascertained for two or more members with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder, genotyped with some unaffected relatives; a patient-based family collection with no exposure basis.

label: Multiethnic Cohort Study of Diet and Health
exposures: diet
quote: The authors describe the design and implementation of a large multiethnic cohort established to study diet and cancer in the United States.
note: A population-based cohort of adults in Hawaii and Los Angeles enrolled through a quantitative food frequency questionnaire to study diet and cancer, like EPIC; a diet-and-cancer cohort on both counts.

label: Multiple Environmental and Genetic Assessment of Risk Factors for Venous Thrombosis
quote: All participants filled in a standardised questionnaire on risk factors for venous thrombosis such as family history of thrombosis, pregnancy, and oral contraceptive use in the year before the index date.
note: A population-based case-control study of patients with a first venous thrombosis recruited through anticoagulation clinics; the 'environmental' risk factors in its name are non-genetic ones such as oral contraceptives, pregnancy and family history, not environmental agents.

label: National Health Service Blood and Transplant
quote: Between mid-2012 and mid-2014, blood donors aged 18 years and older were recruited at 25 centres of England’s National Health Service Blood and Transplant (NHSBT).
note: The blood-donor service whose donors (the INTERVAL participants) form the sample: healthy unselected donors, so neither an exposure nor a disease cohort.

label: National Study of Colorectal Cancer Genetics
note: A national collection of colorectal cancer cases with spouse or partner controls assembled to find susceptibility alleles; a patient collection with no exposure basis.

label: Netherlands Twin Registry
quote: The Netherlands Twin Register (NTR) was established around 1987 by the Department of Biological Psychology at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and recruits approximately 40% of new-born twins or higher-order multiples in the Netherlands for longitudinal research.
note: A twin registry recruiting twins and their relatives for longitudinal research on health, development and behaviour in general; twin registries are out of scope on both counts.

label: New England-based Case-Control Study of Ovarian Cancer
note: A population-based case-control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in New England; the cases are patients with one cancer, and the risk factors studied (such as intrauterine device use) are not environmental exposures.

label: Gastroparesis Clinical Research Consortium cohort
note: Gastroparesis patients from the NIDDK-sponsored consortium of tertiary gastrointestinal centres; a patient series with no exposure basis.

label: Nijmegen Biomedical Study
quote: The NBS was originally established to obtain a universal reference population to be used for studies of genetic variation, lifestyle and environmental exposures in relation to traits or diseases of interest.
note: Population-based reference cohort of adult residents of Nijmegen, established as a universal control population; lifestyle and environmental exposures are named only as one of many uses of a general reference sample, not as a design purpose, and no disease defines it.

label: Northern Ireland Cohort for Longitudinal Study of Ageing
quote: NICOLA is a longitudinal panel of 8283 participants representative of an ‘eligible population’ defined as community dwelling adults aged ≥50 years living in private households in NI, broadly equivalent in sample size to both TILDA3 and ELSA2.
note: Representative panel of community-dwelling adults aged 50 and over in Northern Ireland studied for ageing, health and social circumstances; a general ageing cohort with no exposure or disease basis.

label: Northern Sweden Population Health Study
quote: The Northern Sweden Population Health Study (NSPHS) was conducted to provide a health survey of the communities of Karesuando and Soppero, County of Norrbotten, Sweden.
note: Health survey of the whole population of two sub-arctic parishes in Norrbotten, described as studying the medical consequences of lifestyle and genetics in general; neither an exposure nor a disease selects the participants.

label: Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort study
quote: MoBa is a Norwegian population-based longitudinal cohort study of around 114,500 children, 95,000 mothers and 75,000 fathers.
note: General population birth cohort recruiting pregnant women at routine ultrasound across Norway. The Exposome Catalogue entry gives its purpose as estimating exposure-outcome associations in the broad epidemiological sense, but nothing in the design centres on environmental agents or on one disease.

label: Orkney Complex Disease Study
quote: The Orkney Complex Disease Study (ORCADES) is a family-based study that seeks to identify genetic factors influencing cardiovascular and other disease risks in the isolated archipelago of the Orkney Isles in northern Scotland.
note: Family-based population cohort of people with Orcadian grandparents, aged 16 to 100, studied for genetic factors in cardiovascular and other complex-disease risk; the purpose is broad (complex disease generally), so it is neither a disease nor an exposure cohort.

label: Outcome Reduction With Initial Glargine Intervention Trial
quote: People aged > or = 50 years with evidence of CV disease and with IFG, IGT, newly detected or established diabetes (on 0 or 1 oral agent), and a local glycated hemoglobin < 150% of the upper limit of normal for that assay were recruited
note: Randomised trial cohort of people aged 50 or over with cardiovascular disease and dysglycaemia (impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes); the interventions are insulin glargine and omega-3 supplements, which are treatments, not environmental exposures.

label: Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium
quote: The array was used to genotype ovarian cancer cases and controls from multiple studies participating in the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium, of which 54,747 passes QC.
note: Consortium of ovarian cancer case-control studies pooling cases and controls for genetic and epidemiological risk-factor research; its members are ovarian cancer studies, so it is a disease aggregation and not an exposure one.

label: Oxford Biobank
quote: The OBB is a random, population-based recruitment of healthy participants between the ages of 30 and 50 years from the Oxfordshire general population (approximately 800 000 inhabitants).
note: Random population-based biobank of healthy 30 to 50 year olds in Oxfordshire, built for recall by genotype or phenotype; the cohort profile frames it as a resource for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and chronic non-communicable disease mechanisms in general, which is a broad purpose rather than one disease.

label: PanCareLIFE
quote: Survival after cancer diagnosed during childhood or adolescence continues to improve with new treatments and supportive therapies. Optimal long-term care requires that risks to vulnerable organs are clearly defined and translated into guidelines that are implemented into practice. PanCareLIFE is a pan-European consortium that addresses survivorship issues comprising fertility, hearing impairment and quality of life.
note: Consortium of European cohorts of survivors of cancer diagnosed in childhood or adolescence, studying treatment-related fertility impairment, ototoxicity and quality of life; the participants are cancer patients, and the exposures studied (alkylating agents, radiotherapy) are medical treatments, so it is not an environmental exposure cohort.

label: Parkinson Environment and Gene
exposures: pesticide exposure | traffic-related air pollution
quote: The study included 634 cases and 733 controls (eFigure 1 in Supplement 1) with demographic (self-reported gender, race/ethnicity) and pesticide exposure data (eMethods in Supplement 1).
note: Population-based case-control study of Parkinson disease in central California, named for environment and genes, funded by NIEHS and built around residential pesticide and traffic-related air pollution exposure data on every participant; the cases have Parkinson disease, and the design centres on environmental exposures, though no sentence read states that purpose in so many words.

label: People of the British Isles
quote: In this study, we describe the collection of a cohort of rural UK samples (The People of the British Isles), aimed at providing a well-characterised UK-control population that can be used as a resource by the research community, as well as providing a fine-scale genetic information on the British population.
note: Collection of rural UK volunteers with four grandparents from the same area, built as a control population and for fine-scale population structure; no exposure or disease selects them.

label: Physical Activity and Nutrition in Children Study
exposures: physical activity | diet
quote: The Physical Activity and Nutrition in Children (PANIC) Study is an ongoing 8-year controlled physical activity and dietary intervention study in a large population sample of children who have been followed retrospectively since pregnancy and prospectively until adolescence and will finally be followed until early adulthood
note: Population sample of Kuopio schoolchildren followed from age 7 to 9 into adulthood in a controlled physical activity and dietary intervention study; the lifestyle exposures diet and physical activity are its main subject (as an intervention rather than an observed exposure, hence medium confidence), and no disease defines it.

label: Population-based Colonoscopy study
quote: The Population-based Colonoscopy (PopCol) study is a cohort of Swedish-born individuals from Stockholm, Sweden, which includes an omics-rich set of participants with available data from bowel symptoms questionnaires, gastroenterology visits, and biospecimens.
note: Population-based sample of Swedish-born Stockholm residents examined by colonoscopy with bowel-symptom questionnaires, assembled to assess normal bowel habits in the general adult population; not selected by disease or exposure.

label: Precocious Coronary Artery Disease Study
quote: CHD cases were recruited from four European countries (UK, Italy, Sweden and Germany) between 2004 and 2008
note: Case-control collection of coronary heart disease cases with an affected sibling, identified from disease registries in four European countries, with population controls; a coronary disease patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Pressioni Arteriose Monitorate E Loro Associazionie
quote: Studies in hypertensive patients suggest that ambulatory blood pressure (BP) is prognostically superior to office BP. Much less information is available in the general population, however. Obtaining this information was the purpose of the Pressioni Arteriose Monitorate e Loro Associazioni (PAMELA) study.
note: Representative sample of the general population of Monza with office, home and ambulatory blood pressure and follow-up of cardiovascular deaths, set up to test the prognostic value of blood pressure measurements; a general population cohort whose stated purpose is hypertension and cardiovascular risk, with no exposure basis.

label: Prospective Investigation of the Vasculature in Uppsala Seniors
quote: The PIVUS study is a population-based study of the cardiovascular health in the elderly [28].
note: Random sample of 70 year olds from the Uppsala community register followed to see whether vascular structure and function predict cardiovascular events; a general population cohort whose stated purpose is cardiovascular disease, with no exposure basis.

label: Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension
quote: We combined three existing GWAS datasets (hereafter referred to as Kiel3, CASP4 and WTCCC25) with two independent European-descent case-control datasets genotyped on the Immunochip: the Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension (PAGE: 3,580 cases and 5,902 controls) and the Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium (GAPC: 2,997 cases and 9,183 controls)
note: Case-control collection of 3,580 psoriasis cases and 5,902 controls of European descent genotyped on the Immunochip; a psoriasis patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Psychiatric GWAS Consortium
quote: The Psychiatric GWAS Consortium was founded with the aim of conducting statistically rigorous and comprehensive GWAS meta-analyses for five major psychiatric disorders: ADHD, autism, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and schizophrenia.
note: Consortium pooling case-control GWAS datasets for five psychiatric disorders; its members are patient collections for these disorders, so it is a disease aggregation and not an exposure one.

label: Research on Adolescent Development and Relationships
quote: Participants were recruited via 230 randomly selected elementary schools from several medium-sized cities in the center of the Netherlands.
note: Dutch adolescent development project combining the RADAR-Young and RADAR-Old cohorts, recruited through randomly selected schools and followed with annual questionnaires on relationships with parents, friends and partners; neither an exposure nor a disease defines it.

label: Rotterdam Study
quote: The Rotterdam Study (RS) is a prospective, population-based cohort study of determinants of chronic diseases in older adults (7).
note: Prospective population-based cohort of middle-aged and older residents of the Ommoord district of Rotterdam studying chronic diseases across many organ systems; a broad-purpose general population cohort, so neither a disease nor an exposure cohort.

label: Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean asthma study
quote: Recruitment was performed through probands with a specific asthma phenotype. The collection includes 1394 individuals distributed in 271 families.
note: Familial collection from the Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean founder population recruited through asthma probands, including affected members and their relatives, for the genetics of asthma and allergy; one paper stratified it by proximity to aluminium and pulp industries, but the cohort was not built around that exposure.

label: Sahlgrenska Academy Study on Ischemic Stroke
quote: These participants included 600 cases with ischaemic stroke at ages 18 to 69 years and 600 controls matched for age and sex from the Sahlgrenska Academy Study on Ischemic Stroke (SAHLSIS 28 )
note: Case-control collection of patients aged 18 to 69 with acute ischaemic stroke recruited consecutively at the Sahlgrenska stroke unit in Gothenburg, with matched population controls and longitudinal follow-up; an ischaemic stroke patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: SardiNIA Study of Aging
quote: The SardiNIA project is a longitudinal study comprising 6,602 general population individuals
note: General population longitudinal study of residents aged 14 and over from four towns in the Lanusei valley of Sardinia, set up to study genetic influences on ageing and age-related traits; neither a disease nor an exposure defines it.

label: Scania Diabetes Registry
quote: The Scania Diabetes Registry contains over 7000 diabetes patients recruited at hospitals in Scania, Sweden as from 1996.
note: Hospital-based registry of over 7000 diabetes patients in Scania, Sweden, with clinical follow-up and samples for classifying diabetes subgroups and predicting complications; a diabetes patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Shanghai Study
quote: Patients with gallbladder carcinoma (GBC), the most aggressive malignancy of the biliary tract, have a poor prognosis. Here, we report our identification of somatic mutations of GBCs in 57 tumor-normal pairs by use of a combination of exome sequencing and ultra-deep sequencing of cancer-related genes.
note: Series of gallbladder carcinoma patients at Xinhua Hospital, Shanghai, whose paired tumour and normal samples were exome-sequenced for somatic mutations; a tumour patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Short Course Oncology Treatment trial
quote: The SCOT study was an international, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial done at 244 centres. Patients aged 18 years or older with high-risk stage II and stage III colorectal cancer underwent central randomisation with minimisation for centre, choice of regimen, sex, disease site, N stage, T stage, and the starting dose of capecitabine.
note: A randomised adjuvant-chemotherapy trial whose participants all had high-risk stage II or III colorectal cancer; the only intervention is treatment, so it is a disease cohort and not an exposure cohort.

label: Simons Simplex Collection
quote: The Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) is a rigorously characterized set of data drawn from 2,700 families, designed to enrich the discovery of rare and de novo events in autism spectrum disorders.
note: Families each recruited for a child with an autism spectrum disorder (parents and siblings unaffected), assembled for autism genetics; no environmental exposure in the design.

label: Singapore Chinese Study
quote: Mucosa specimens from 1,000 sporadic Chinese CRC patients (defined as age 50 or more at date of operation and without dominant family history of FAP and HNPCC) archived over the past ten years were selected as cases for the study.
note: A colorectal cancer case-control series of Singapore Chinese (1,000 CRC patients resected at Singapore General Hospital, 1,000 matched healthy controls) built for CRC susceptibility genetics; no exposure basis.

label: SORCE
quote: A multi-centre phase III double-blind placebo-controlled study designed to examine the efficacy and tolerability of sorafenib (Nexavar) in patients with resected (total or partial) primary renal cell carcinoma (RCC) at high or intermediate risk of relapse
note: A randomised trial of adjuvant sorafenib in patients with resected renal cell carcinoma; the drug is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Spit for Science
exposures: alcohol use | related substance use
quote: We describe an effort to create a university-wide research project aimed at understanding how genes and environments impact alcohol use and related substance use and mental health outcomes across time in college students.
note: A whole-freshman-class student cohort whose stated purpose is genetic and environmental influences on alcohol and other substance use and on mental health, so alcohol use is its main subject (like a smoking-behaviour consortium) and its outcome family is substance use and emotional health problems; participants are an unselected student population, so the disease role is population study of disease rather than patients.

label: Sweden Bipolar Disorder Cohort
quote: Across the two waves, SWEBIC recruited 8580 individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder, 89 percent from BipoläR.
note: A Swedish case collection of people diagnosed with bipolar disorder (from the BipoläR quality register and clinical services) with unaffected controls, built for bipolar disorder genetics; no exposure basis.

label: Swedish Twin Registry
exposures: smoking | alcohol consumption
quote: The Swedish Twin Registry (STR), which today has developed into a unique resource, was first established in the late 1950s to study the importance of smoking and alcohol consumption on cancer and cardiovascular diseases whilst controlling for genetic propensity to disease.
note: A national twin registry founded expressly to study smoking and alcohol consumption in relation to cancer and cardiovascular disease, which satisfies the stated-purpose test for exposures even though its focus has since broadened to most common complex diseases; as a twin registry with a broad disease remit it is not a disease cohort.

label: Taiwan Type 2 Diabetes Study
quote: A total of 2,798 unrelated individuals with T2D, age >20 years, were recruited from China Medical University Hospital (CMUH), Taichung, Taiwan; Chia-Yi Christian Hospital (CYCH), Chia-Yi, Taiwan; and National Taiwan University Hospital (NTU), Taipei, Taiwan.
note: A Han Chinese type 2 diabetes case-control collection from three Taiwanese hospitals assembled for a T2D GWAS; no exposure basis.

label: TEENs of Attica: Genes and Environment
quote: The TEENAGE study is a cross-sectional study comprising healthy Greek adolescents.
note: A school-based sample of healthy Greek adolescents studied for anthropometric and pubertal traits; despite 'Genes and Environment' in its name, dietary data are collected among many variables with no exposure stated as the design purpose, and the participants are healthy.

label: The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
quote: The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) is a panel study of a representative cohort of men and women living in England aged ≥50 years.
note: A representative panel study of ageing in adults aged 50 and over in England, multidisciplinary in scope; neither exposure-defined nor about one disease.

label: The Fenland Study
exposures: lifestyle factors
quote: The Fenland study is designed to investigate the interaction between genetic and lifestyle factors in determining diabetes, obesity, and related metabolic disorders.
note: A population-based Cambridgeshire cohort whose stated design is the interaction of genetic and lifestyle factors in diabetes, obesity and related metabolic disorders: lifestyle exposure is a stated design purpose (the bundle shows habitual diet measured; the source names only 'lifestyle factors'), and the outcome is one disease family, so it is a population study of metabolic disease.

label: The Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren
quote: HGF-Study The HGF GWA study (center 1: Wichmann, Sauter, center 2: Bickeböller, Rosenberger, center 3: Risch, Chang-Claude) was made up of three independent German studies as detailed below: In total 506 incident lung cancer cases (LUCY-study: n=305, Heidelberg lung cancer case-control study: n=201) were compared to 480 popula-tion controls (KORA surveys KORA).
note: The catalogue tag denotes the Helmholtz (HGF) lung cancer GWAS, a German lung cancer case-control collection (LUCY and Heidelberg cases against KORA population controls), so it is classified as a lung cancer patient cohort; the COHO definition instead describes the research organisation, and no exposure defines the sample.

label: The MANOLIS cohort
quote: Here, we perform whole-genome-sequence-based association analysis between 257 cardiometabolic disease-related serum protein levels9 and 13,419,876 single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in a population-based cohort (MANOLIS), and assess colocalization, causation and predictive power of protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) in cardiometabolic disease.
note: A population-based isolate cohort from the Mylopotamos villages of Crete used for genetic association with cardiometabolic and other complex traits; neither exposure-defined nor selected for a disease.

label: The Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset
quote: The individual GWAS data sets from Iceland and the Netherlands were adjusted for genomic inflation before inclusion in the meta-analysis.
note: The Dutch data set is one of the six abdominal aortic aneurysm GWAS data sets (4972 AAA cases in all, with Rotterdam Study controls) in the AAA meta-analysis, so it is an AAA case-control collection; its own composition is given only in an online table, hence medium confidence, and nothing suggests an exposure basis.

label: The Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma
quote: The Swedish/Norwegian GWAS5 was based on 1,668 and 157 MM patients from the Swedish National Myeloma Biobank (Skåne University Hospital, Lund, Sweden) and the Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma (Trondheim, Norway), respectively.
note: A biobank of multiple myeloma patients in Trondheim providing cases for myeloma susceptibility GWAS; no exposure basis.

label: The Pakistan Risk Of Myocardial Infarction Study
quote: By March 2009, PROMIS had recruited over 5,000 cases of first-ever confirmed acute myocardial infarction (MI) and over 5,000 matched controls aged 30-80 years.
note: A Pakistani case-control study of first acute myocardial infarction with matched controls; lifestyle is recorded as one class of determinant among genetic and biochemical ones, not as the design's exposure focus.

label: The Secondary Manifestations of ARTerial disease study
quote: The Second Manifestations of ARTerial disease (SMART) study is a single-centre prospective cohort study among patients, newly referred to the hospital with (1) clinically manifest atherosclerotic vessel disease, or (2) marked risk factors for atherosclerosis.
note: A hospital cohort of patients referred with manifest atherosclerotic vascular disease (or marked atherosclerosis risk factors, an at-risk minority) followed for cardiovascular events; disease-based recruitment, no exposure basis.

label: The Hellenic study of Interactions between Single nucleotide polymorphisms and Eating in Atherosclerosis Susceptibility
exposures: eating
quote: The study population was drawn from the THISEAS (The Hellenic Study of Interactions between Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms and Eating in Atherosclerosis Susceptibility) database, constituting a case-control cohort.
note: A Greek coronary artery disease case-control collection, so a disease cohort of CAD patients; the exposure verdict rests on the study's name alone, which states its subject as interactions between SNPs and eating in atherosclerosis susceptibility, since the bundled papers use it only as a CAD case-control set and describe no dietary design.

label: Treating to New Targets
quote: A total of 10,001 patients with clinically evident CHD and LDL cholesterol levels of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) were randomly assigned to double-blind therapy and received either 10 mg or 80 mg of atorvastatin per day.
note: A randomised statin trial in patients with clinically evident stable coronary heart disease; the intervention is a medication, not an exposure.

label: Twins Early Development Study
quote: The Twins Early Development Study (TEDS) is a longitudinal twin study that recruited over 16,000 twin-pairs born between 1994 and 1996 in England and Wales through national birth records.
note: A population twin birth cohort recruited from national birth records to study cognitive, behavioural and emotional development; an EGA subset was screened for autism, but the cohort itself is neither exposure-defined nor about one disease.

label: Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium
quote: The Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium (T1DGC) is an international project whose primary aims are to: (a) discover genes that modify type 1 diabetes risk; and (b) expand upon the existing genetic resources for type 1 diabetes research. The initial goal was to collect 2500 affected sibling pair (ASP) families worldwide.
note: A consortium collecting affected sib-pair families, trios, cases and controls for type 1 diabetes genetics, so an aggregation of type 1 diabetes patient collections; no exposure basis.

label: UK Adult Twin Register
quote: The UK Adult Twin Registry (or TwinsUK Registry) is a cohort of volunteer adult twins from all over the United Kingdom.
note: A registry of volunteer adult twins studied for ageing and complex disorders in general; a twin registry with a broad remit, so neither an exposure nor a disease cohort.

label: UK Biobank
quote: As described in the manuscript, the MRC and Wellcome Trust played a key role in the decision to establish UK Biobank, a large, population-based, prospective, open access resource that would allow detailed investigations of the genetic and environmental determinants of the diseases of middle and old age.
note: A population-based biobank of half a million UK adults for the genetic and environmental determinants of diseases of middle and old age in general; environmental determinants are mentioned as one broad class among many and the disease remit is broad, so no on both counts despite its listing in the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue.

label: UK Brain Expression Consortium
quote: Central nervous system (CNS) tissues originating from 134 control individuals was collected by the Medical Research Council (MRC) Sudden Death Brain and Tissue Bank, Edinburgh, UK (Millar et al. 2007), and the Sun Health Research Institute (SHRI) an affiliate of Sun Health Corporation, USA (Beach et al. 2008).
note: A consortium of post-mortem brain tissue from neuropathologically normal control donors used for expression QTL mapping; donors were selected as neurologically healthy, so neither an exposure nor a disease cohort.

label: UK Childhood Cancer Study
exposures: radon gas | terrestrial gamma radiation | electric and magnetic fields
quote: Information about both groups of children (with and without cancer) has been obtained from parental questionnaires, general practitioners' and hospital records, and from measurement of the extent of exposure to radon gas, terrestrial gamma radiation, and electric and magnetic fields.
note: A national case-control study of all children with cancer in Great Britain 1991-1998 and matched population controls, set up to find the causes of childhood cancer with measurement of radon, gamma radiation and electromagnetic field exposure built into its design; so a cancer patient cohort that is also designed to study exposures.

label: UK Household Longitudinal Study
quote: The UKHLS is a longitudinal survey of the members of approximately 40,000 households in the UK
note: Understanding Society is a general household panel survey of the UK population covering education, employment, income, health and family life; it selects on neither an exposure nor a disease and served as general population controls.

label: UK Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium
quote: With the support of Crohn’s and Colitis UK, the UK Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium has been at the front of this research – building a vast database of genetic and clinical data from patients across the UK.
note: A consortium of UK inflammatory bowel disease patient collections (Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis cases) assembled for genetic studies; no environmental exposure defines it.

label: Viking Health Study
quote: The Viking Health Study—Shetland (hereafter VIKING1) is a geographically defined cohort with grandparents from the Shetland Isles, north of Scotland, which seeks to identify genetic factors influencing cardiovascular and other disease risk54.
note: A population-isolate genetic cohort of Shetland volunteers with a broad remit (risk factors for common diseases such as heart disease, diabetes, glaucoma and stroke); not selected by exposure or by any one disease.

label: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
quote: We describe a joint GWA study (using the Affymetrix GeneChip 500K Mapping Array Set) undertaken in the British population, which has examined approximately 2,000 individuals for each of 7 major diseases and a shared set of approximately 3,000 controls.
note: A consortium of disease-specific case collections (seven common diseases in the 2007 study, further diseases in the member case-control studies) with shared population controls; classified by the patient collections it aggregates, with no exposure basis.

label: Basquecolon cohort
quote: Basque-colon cohort included 873 participants with colon cancer, biobanked between 20092019. Participants were diagnosed and/or treated according to usual clinical practice in the Donostia University Hospital, San Sebastian, Spain
note: A hospital case series of colon cancer patients (with comparison participants) used as a colorectal cancer PRS validation set; no exposure basis.

label: INTERVAL study
quote: INTERVAL is a randomised trial of whole blood donors enrolled from all 25 static centres of NHS Blood and Transplant.
note: A randomised trial of healthy whole-blood donors comparing donation intervals; the intervention is a procedure, not an environmental exposure, and donors have no disease.

label: CONVERGE
quote: Here, using low-coverage whole-genome sequencing of 5,303 Chinese women with recurrent MDD selected to reduce phenotypic heterogeneity, and 5,337 controls screened to exclude MDD, we identified, and subsequently replicated in an independent sample, two loci contributing to risk of MDD on chromosome 10
note: A case-control collection of Han Chinese women with recurrent major depressive disorder and screened controls; no exposure basis.

label: Gene-Environmental Interaction and phenotype study
quote: In this study, we used data from the Gene-Environment of Interaction and phenotype (GENIE) cohort, and the Health and Prevention Enhancement (H-PEACE) cohort, at the Seoul National University Hospital Healthcare System Gangnam Center, where comprehensive health check-ups and screening are done in Korean populations.
