note: Whole-genome sequencing cohort of patients with rare diseases (or extreme quantitative traits), their affected relatives and controls, enrolled at NHS hospitals for diagnosis and gene discovery; a patient cohort across 15 rare disease domains, not exposure-based.

label: Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study of Ageing
quote: They will be reassessed at 18-month intervals in order to determine the predictive utility of various biomarkers, cognitive parameters and lifestyle factors as indicators of AD, and as predictors of future cognitive decline.
note: Longitudinal volunteer cohort of people over 60 with Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment and healthy controls recruited for prospective research into Alzheimer's disease; lifestyle factors are one class of candidate predictor alongside imaging and biomarkers, not the cohort's defining or main subject, so not an exposure cohort.

label: PopGen Biobank
quote: PopGen currently pursues recruitment, sampling and processing activities in close collaboration with a multitude of clinical partners, covering cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric and environmental diseases.
note: A population-based biobank in northern Germany that ascertains patients across cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric and other complex diseases together with population controls. A multi-disease genetic-epidemiology resource with no exposure design, so neither an exposure cohort nor a cohort of one disease.

label: Diabetic Nephropathy Cohort
note: Outpatients with type 2 diabetes recruited at a Singapore diabetes centre and followed for diabetic nephropathy and cardiovascular events; a patient cohort, with no exposure-based selection.

label: Singapore Study of Macro-Angiopathy and Micro-Vascular Reactivity in Type 2 Diabetes
note: A prospective cohort of patients with type 2 diabetes recruited in northern Singapore to study vascular function and diabetes complications; a patient cohort, not exposure-defined.

label: Women's Health Initiative
quote: The Women's Health Initiative (WHI) is a large and complex clinical investigation of strategies for the prevention and control of some of the most common causes of morbidity and mortality among postmenopausal women, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and osteoporotic fractures.
note: Postmenopausal women enrolled into prevention trials (low-fat eating pattern, hormone therapy, calcium and vitamin D) or a parallel observational study, followed for cancer, cardiovascular disease and fractures. The dietary arm is an assigned intervention rather than an exposure-defined design, and the purpose spans several disease families, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Study of Health in Pomerania-TREND
quote: To identify determinants of the anti-TSST-1 antibody response, we examined 976 participants of the German population-based epidemiological Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP-TREND-0).
note: A population-based sample of adults from Western Pomerania recruited as the second SHIP cohort for general health research; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study
quote: KoGES includes the community-based Ansan and Ansung study, the urban community-based health examinee study, and the rural community-based cardiovascular disease association study.
note: A consortium of Korean population-based cohorts and a national biobank set up to study the genetic and environmental aetiology of common complex diseases. Environmental exposure data are collected among many variables, but the design is a general-purpose population resource, not an exposure or single-disease study.

label: Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study
quote: The NEO study is a population-based, prospective cohort study that includes 6,673 individuals aged 45–65 years, with an oversampling of individuals with overweight or obesity.
note: A population-based cohort from the Leiden area in which people with a BMI of 27 or higher were eligible, oversampling overweight and obesity, designed to trace pathways to obesity-related diseases. Participants were selected for a disease-risk state (obesity counting as a disease), not for an environmental exposure.

label: Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention
note: Middle-aged adults enriched for a parental history of Alzheimer's disease dementia, followed for preclinical Alzheimer's disease; a cohort selected for disease risk, with no exposure basis.

label: Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
note: The Clinical Core longitudinal cohort of the Wisconsin ADRC, recruiting people with mild Alzheimer's disease or mild cognitive impairment alongside healthy controls and middle-aged adults with a parental history of Alzheimer's disease; a disease cohort of patients and at-risk relatives, not exposure-defined.

label: Food Chain Plus
quote: The Food Chain Plus (FoCus) cohort was launched in 2011 for population-based research related to metabolic inflammation.
note: A Kiel-region cohort of which three quarters were drawn at random from residents' registers and one quarter were patients with metabolic inflammation from the university obesity outpatient centre, set up to study metabolic inflammation and the diseases it drives. Nutrition profiling is one of many data layers rather than an exposure-centred design, so the exposure verdict is no; the single-pathology purpose and patient component make it a disease cohort.

label: Amish Complex Disease Research Program
quote: To date, over 7000 Amish adults have participated in one or more of our studies as part of the Amish Complex Disease Research Program72.
note: A University of Maryland research programme collecting studies of the Old Order Amish founder population of Lancaster County on the genetics of complex diseases (osteoporosis, cardiometabolic traits, longevity). Its members are population and family studies across many diseases with no exposure design, so both verdicts are no.

label: BioVU
quote: In 2007, VUMC launched a biobank, BioVU, and the BioVU Consent form is provided to patients in the outpatient clinic environments at VUMC.
note: A practice-based biobank of DNA from leftover clinical blood of Vanderbilt patients linked to de-identified health records; donors are unselected for any disease or exposure.

label: Southall and Brent Revisited
quote: SABRE was set up in 1988 as a tri-ethnic longitudinal cohort study to examine ethnic differences in chronic disease.
note: A population-based tri-ethnic London cohort set up in 1988 to compare cardiovascular disease and diabetes between European, South Asian and African Caribbean people, described more loosely in a 2024 paper as a study of ethnic differences in chronic disease. Taken as a population study of one cardiometabolic disease family; no exposure basis.

label: Gut-and-Liver Axis in Alcoholic Liver Fibrosis
exposures: harmful drinking
quote: The GALA–ALD cohort is a diagnostic-test cohort of consecutively recruited patients with a history of harmful drinking.
note: Consecutively recruited patients with a history of harmful drinking and early alcohol-related liver disease, with matched healthy controls, from Odense within the EU GALAXY consortium. Selection on harmful alcohol use makes it an exposure-defined cohort, and the participants are patients with alcohol-related liver disease.

label: Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study
note: A population-based cohort of Finnish children and adolescents sampled in 1980 and followed into adulthood to relate childhood cardiovascular risk factors to preclinical cardiovascular disease, as its name states. A general population cohort devoted to one disease family; no exposure basis.

label: Study of Colorectal Cancer in Scotland
note: A population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in Scotland whose cases are followed for survival; the participants of interest are colorectal cancer patients, with no exposure-based selection.

label: China Kadoorie Biobank
quote: The China Kadoorie Biobank (CKB) is a population-based prospective cohort of >512,000 adults recruited from 2004 to 2008 from 10 geographically diverse regions across China.
note: A population-based prospective biobank of half a million adults from ten regions of China studying many diseases and risk factors; no exposure or disease selection.

label: All of Us Research Program
quote: The All of Us Research Program plans to enroll a diverse group of at least 1 million persons in the United States in order to accelerate biomedical research and improve health.
note: A national precision-medicine cohort enrolling a million diverse US adults with questionnaires, health records and biospecimens; a general population resource with no exposure or disease selection.

label: BioMe Biobank
quote: A snLVEF genetic risk score (GRS) was applied and cases of snLVEF were identified in 486 754 individuals across two population-based cohorts (BioMe Biobank and UK Biobank).
note: An electronic health record-linked biobank enrolling patients of the Mount Sinai Health System non-selectively; a general biobank with no exposure or disease selection.

label: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study
note: A prospective cohort of Black and White young adults recruited in 1985-1986 at four US centres and followed into midlife for the development of coronary and cardiovascular risk factors and disease, as its name states. A general population cohort devoted to one disease family; not exposure-defined.

label: Health for Life in Singapore
quote: Participants were recruited from the Singapore general population11,13,14.
note: A population-based multi-ethnic cohort of 10,004 Singapore residents for precision-medicine research on diverse diseases; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Cleveland Family Study
note: A family study built around index probands with laboratory-confirmed obstructive sleep apnoea, their relatives and neighbourhood control families, designed to study the familial basis of sleep-disordered breathing. A disease cohort of patients and their at-risk relatives; no exposure basis.

label: deCODE genetics Icelandic cohort
quote: This study is based on whole-genome sequence data from the whole blood of 15,220 Icelanders participating in various disease projects at deCODE genetics.
note: A population sample of Icelanders recruited through deCODE's many disease-specific projects and its general-population deCODE Health Study, used for genome-wide studies of diseases and traits at large. A multi-disease national resource with no exposure design, so both verdicts are no.

label: PainOMICS Retrospective Study
note: A multicentre retrospective case-control study of patients with chronic low back pain and pain-free controls run by the EU PainOMICS project; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: The Pomak cohort
quote: We use whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to capture the entire allele frequency spectrum in 2,893 samples from two Greek population-based cohorts, MANOLIS and Pomak.
note: A population-based cohort of adult volunteers from the isolated Pomak villages of northern Greece recruited within the Hellenic Isolated Cohorts to study the genetics of complex traits; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
quote: Participants in the GERA cohort were recruited from the adult membership of the KPNC health plan, a large integrated health care system that provides comprehensive medical services to four million members.
note: GERA is a general cohort of adult Kaiser Permanente Northern California health-plan members within RPGEH, genotyped as a resource for GWAS of diverse traits and conditions; participants were selected neither for an exposure nor for a disease.

label: Correlated Expression and Disease Association Research
quote: We collected peripheral blood as well as intestinal biopsies (ileum, transverse colon, rectum) from 323 healthy Europeans visiting the Academic Hospital of the University of Liège as part of a national screening campaign for colon cancer.
note: CEDAR is a panel of about 320 healthy adults recruited at a colon-cancer screening campaign in Liège whose blood-cell and gut transcriptomes serve as an eQTL resource; it was built to interpret IBD risk loci, but its participants are healthy volunteers rather than patients, so it is not a disease cohort, and no exposure defines it.

label: Generation Scotland: Scottish Family Health Study
quote: Generation Scotland (GS) is a large family-based cohort study established as a longitudinal resource for research into the genetic, lifestyle and environmental determinants of physical and mental health.
note: Generation Scotland is a family-based general-population cohort recruited through general practices as a broad resource for physical and mental health research; environment is one of many determinants and no single disease is its purpose.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy
quote: In the first phase of GENOA (Phase I: 1996–2001), sibships with at least two adults with clinically diagnosed essential hypertension before age 60 were recruited, and all siblings in the sibship were invited to participate regardless of hypertension status.
note: GENOA recruited sibships ascertained on at least two siblings with clinically diagnosed essential hypertension before age 60, to find genes for blood pressure and hypertensive target-organ damage; recruitment is by disease (hypertensive sibships, normotensive siblings included), and no environmental exposure defines the cohort.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohorts
quote: We used data from two general population birth cohort studies, Northern Finland Birth Cohorts 1966 and 1986 (NFBC1966 and NFBC1986).
note: The Northern Finland Birth Cohorts programme collects two general-population birth cohorts (1966 and 1986) followed from the fetal period for health and well-being; neither an exposure nor a disease defines them.

label: Taiwan Biobank
quote: To advance epidemiological and biomedical research, Taiwan launched its own biobank, the Taiwan Biobank (TWB), in 2012, which prospectively collected a wide variety of lifestyle behaviors, environmental risk factors, and family history of common, complex diseases in the general Taiwanese population and measured genetic information in the biobank participants.
note: Taiwan Biobank is a prospective population biobank of volunteers from the general Taiwanese population; it records lifestyle and environmental exposures among many variables without exposure being its design purpose, and it targets no single disease.

label: GeneRISK study
quote: We use data from the prospective GeneRISK cohort46 whose principal aim is to assess the impact of communication of genetic risk information of CVD to study participants.
note: GeneRISK is a general-population cohort of Finnish adults (population register, occupational health customers, blood donors) set up to test how returning polygenic and clinical risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease changes health behaviour; participants were not selected for disease, but the cohort's stated purpose is one disease family, so it is a population study of cardiovascular disease; no exposure defines it.

label: Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span
quote: We designed a multidisciplinary, community-based, prospective longitudinal epidemiologic study among socioeconomically diverse African Americans and Whites.
note: HANDLS is an area-probability community sample of Baltimore adults stratified by age, sex, race and poverty status to study how race and socioeconomic status shape age-related health disparities; socioeconomic status alone is not an environmental exposure under these rules, and its health outcomes are broad.

label: Mount Sinai Crohn's and Colitis Registry
quote: Patients with UC (n=484) or CD (n=464) and HCs (ages 18+, n=365) were recruited as part of a cross-sectional study, the Mount Sinai Crohn’s and Colitis Registry (MSCCR), between December 2013 and September 2016 from the outpatient and endoscopy units of the Mount Sinai Hospital.
note: MSCCR is a registry of about 1,500 adults recruited at endoscopy at Mount Sinai Hospital, mostly patients with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease plus non-IBD controls, for molecular studies of inflammatory bowel disease; a patient series with controls, not an exposure cohort.

label: Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety
quote: The Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety (NESDA, www.nesda.nl) is a longitudinal, multi-site, naturalistic, case-control cohort study set up to examine the etiology, course and consequences of depressive and anxiety disorders.
note: NESDA recruited adults with current or remitted depressive and/or anxiety disorders, at-risk persons and healthy controls from the general population, primary care and mental health care to follow the course of these disorders; a case-control disease cohort with no defining exposure.

label: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study
quote: The Health, Aging, and Body Composition (Health ABC) study11 was a prospective longitudinal observational study designed to assess the association of body composition with physical function and disability in older adults.
note: Health ABC enrolled community-dwelling adults aged 70-79 from Medicare lists and Black residents of Pittsburgh and Memphis to study body composition, functional decline and disability in ageing; a population cohort of older adults with a broad purpose, selected neither for exposure nor for disease.

label: Michigan Genomics Initiative
quote: Here, we describe the Michigan Genomics Initiative (MGI), a single-health-system biobank currently consisting of >91,000 participants recruited primarily during surgical encounters at Michigan Medicine.
note: MGI is a health-system biobank of adult patients consented mainly at surgery, enriched for many diseases but for none in particular; a broad disease-genetics resource, not a cohort of patients with one disease, and no exposure defines it.

label: Immune and Metabolic Markers during Pregnancy and Child Development Study
quote: Although this cohort was ascertained for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other neurodevelopmental disorders (DD), we gained novel insight into how maternal and fetal genetics shape levels of immune mediators in pregnancy.
note: IMPaCT is a case-control study of KPNC mother-child pairs oversampling children later diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder or other developmental delay, with general-population controls, to study maternal immune and metabolic markers in pregnancy; the cases of a case-control study make it a disease cohort, and no environmental exposure defines it.

label: Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology Consortium
quote: Special features of the CHARGE consortium are the large overall sample size, the population-based recruitment of cohort members, the standardized methods of data collection, and the prospective follow-up for clinical events.
note: CHARGE collects large prospective population-based cohorts (AGES, ARIC, CHS, FHS, Rotterdam and later others) for GWAS meta-analysis across many cardiovascular and ageing-related phenotypes; its members are population cohorts and its stated purpose is methodological and broad (heart and ageing research), so it is neither an exposure nor a single-disease aggregation.

label: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study
quote: This study was carried out in 1082 subjects belonging to the Helsinki Birth Cohort Study, which consists of men and women born between 1934 and 1944, in Helsinki, Finland, representing a general population of elderly people.
note: HBCS is a birth cohort of all singletons born in two Helsinki maternity hospitals in 1934-1944, followed to study how early life shapes adult health; a general-population birth cohort, and the persistent-organic-pollutant analysis in one paper is a use of the cohort, not its design.

label: Generation R Study
exposures: environmental determinants | endocrine determinants | lifestyle related determinants | nutritional determinants
quote: Main exposures of interest include environmental, endocrine, genomic (genetic, epigenetic, microbiome), lifestyle related, nutritional and socio-demographic determinants.
note: Generation R is a population-based birth cohort in Rotterdam designed to identify early environmental and genetic causes of growth, development and health, naming environmental, endocrine, lifestyle and nutritional determinants as its main exposures of interest, and it is listed in the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue; its outcomes are broad, so it is not a disease cohort.

label: 500 Functional Genomics
quote: The 500FG cohort is a population-based cohort of healthy individuals of Western European ancestry consisting of 237 males and 296 females with age range of 18-75 years.
note: 500FG is about 500 healthy adult volunteers recruited at Radboudumc to characterise variation in cytokine and immune responses; the host and environmental factors it examines (age, sex, BMI, season, vitamin D) are not environmental exposures in the sense used here, and healthy volunteers are not a disease cohort.

label: MyCode Community Health Initiative
quote: In 2007, Geisinger launched MyCode, a system-wide biobanking program to link samples and EHR data for broad research use.
note: MyCode is a health-system biobank of Geisinger patients consented for broad research use with EHR linkage and genotype and exome data; patients of an integrated health system without selection for one disease or for an exposure.

label: 23andMe research cohort
quote: All participants were drawn from the customer base of 23andMe, Inc., a direct-to-consumer genetics company.
note: The 23andMe research cohort is the company's consenting customer base answering online questionnaires; unselected consumers with no defining exposure or disease.

label: LIFE-Adult-Study
quote: The LIFE-Adult-Study is a population-based cohort study, which has recently completed the baseline examination of 10,000 randomly selected participants from Leipzig, a major city with 550,000 inhabitants in the east of Germany.
note: LIFE-Adult is a random population sample of Leipzig adults deeply phenotyped for major civilization diseases (metabolic, vascular, cognitive, depression, sleep, retinal, allergies); a broad multi-disease purpose in an unselected population, with no defining exposure.

label: Red Blood Cell-Omics Study
quote: As part of the REDS-III RBC-Omics study, a cohort of 12,535 volunteer blood donors were enrolled to donate a unit of blood that was processed into RBC components that were characterized for storage hemolysis parameters.
note: RBC-Omics enrolled about 13,400 volunteer blood donors at four US blood centres to study donor iron metabolism and red-cell storage haemolysis; unselected donors, not a disease or exposure cohort.

label: Corogene Study
quote: Corogene is a prospective, consecutive cohort study of Finnish patients referred for coronary angiography to the Helsinki University Central Hospital between 2006 and 2008.
note: Corogene is a consecutive series of Finnish patients referred for coronary angiography, assembled to study genetic predisposition to coronary heart disease, with its acute coronary syndrome cases forming a case-control sample against FINRISK controls; a patient cohort with no defining exposure.

label: Health 2000 GenMets Study
quote: In the current study, we used the GenMets sample, which includes individuals with metabolic syndrome and matched control subjects drawn from the Health 2000 study.
note: GenMets is a case-control sub-cohort of the Finnish Health 2000 survey of participants with metabolic syndrome and matched controls, genotyped for the genetics of metabolic syndrome; the cases of a case-control study, with no defining exposure.

label: Qatar Metabolomics Study on Diabetes
quote: Inclusion criteria were a primary form of type 2 diabetes (for patients) or an absence of type 2 diabetes (for controls).
note: QMDiab is a cross-sectional case-control study of 374 people with and without type 2 diabetes enrolled at Hamad Medical Corporation in Doha for multi-fluid metabolomics of diabetes; a patient case-control cohort, not an exposure cohort.

label: Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk
quote: Participants came from EA and AA families identified from 1983 to 2006 from probands with a premature coronary disease event before 60 years of age who were identified at the time of hospitalization in any of 10 Baltimore area hospitals.
note: GeneSTAR enrolled the apparently healthy 30-59-year-old siblings of probands hospitalised with a premature coronary disease event before age 60 in Baltimore, to find environmental, phenotypic and genetic causes of premature cardiovascular disease; relatives of patients are an at-risk disease cohort, and the two-week aspirin trial is a medication, not an environmental exposure.

label: Nurses' Health Study
exposures: lifestyle
quote: Over 40 years, these studies have generated long-term, multidimensional data, including lifestyle- and health-related information across the life course and an extensive repository of various biological specimens.
note: A prospective cohort of US registered nurses enrolled in 1976 and followed by questionnaire for lifestyle and other risk factors of major chronic diseases; the nurses were enrolled as reliable reporters, not for an occupational hazard. Lifestyle (diet, smoking, alcohol, activity) is the study's main subject per the definition, but the cached source only says lifestyle data were generated, so the exposure verdict is low confidence; the disease scope is chronic diseases broadly, so it is not a disease cohort.

label: Penn Medicine BioBank
note: An EHR-linked biobank of unselected patients of the University of Pennsylvania Health System recruited in outpatient clinics for genomic discovery across all phenotypes; no exposure and no single disease defines it.

label: Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis
exposures: environmental factors | cigarette smoking
quote: To investigate the inﬂuence of environmental factors on the risk of developing RA and the interaction of these factors with genotype we started an extensive case-control study—the Epidemiological Investigation of RA (EIRA) study.
note: A Swedish population-based case-control study of incident rheumatoid arthritis cases and population controls, started expressly to investigate environmental risk factors (cigarette smoking foremost) and their interaction with genotype; the cases make it a disease cohort and its stated design makes it an exposure cohort.

label: Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health Study
note: A hospital-based cohort of patients referred for coronary angiography in Ludwigshafen, with and without coronary artery disease, followed to study risk factors for cardiovascular disease; environmental factors and chemical exposures are listed among many risk factors, not as the design's centre.

label: Diabetes Heart Study
note: A family study of siblings concordant for type 2 diabetes (plus unaffected relatives) recruited from clinics in North Carolina to study diabetic heart disease and subclinical cardiovascular disease; the affected sib-pairs make it a patient cohort, and no environmental exposure is part of its design.

label: Genetics of Personality Consortium
note: A consortium of about 30 population, twin and family cohorts pooled for GWAS meta-analyses of personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion); personality is a trait, and major depressive disorder status is available only in a few member cohorts as a secondary phenotype, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Genetic Risk Assessment for Chinese Eaglet-T1D
note: A Chinese multicentre paediatric case-control collection of children with type 1 diabetes and controls used to validate polygenic risk scores; the cases make it a disease cohort and no exposure is involved.

label: Academic Medical Center Amsterdam Premature Atherosclerosis Study
note: A prospective cohort of Academic Medical Center Amsterdam patients with symptomatic coronary artery disease before age 51, used for genetic studies of premature atherosclerosis; a patient series with no exposure basis.

label: Bogalusa Heart Study
note: A community-based cohort of children and adolescents of Bogalusa, Louisiana, begun in 1972 to study cardiovascular risk factors and the natural history of cardiovascular disease from early life; a Framingham-type population study of one disease family, with no exposure basis.

label: Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study
note: A family-based longitudinal cohort ascertained through children referred by speech-language pathologists with a speech sound disorder (including childhood apraxia of speech), with their siblings, followed for 25 years; speech sound disorder is a neurodevelopmental (DSM) disorder, so the probands make it a patient cohort, and no exposure is involved.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium
note: A consortium pooling twelve case-control GWAS samples of opioid addiction (Yale-Penn, COGA, deCODE, VIDUS and others); addiction counts as a disease, so it is a patient aggregation, and opioid use is a drug rather than an environmental agent, so it is not an exposure cohort.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Study
note: A prospective cohort of adults with DSM-IV opioid dependence receiving methadone maintenance treatment at Canadian Addiction Treatment Centre clinics in Ontario, studied for genetic and other predictors of treatment outcomes; a patient cohort of an addiction disorder, with no environmental-exposure basis.

label: deCODE Health Study
note: A comprehensively phenotyped general-population sample of Icelanders (enriched for carriers of rare variants) used for genetic association studies of many traits; neither disease nor exposure defines it.

label: Qatar Biobank
note: A population-based prospective biobank of adult Qatari nationals and long-term residents recruited to study the causes and burden of disease in general; environmental and lifestyle factors are measured among many variables, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Reykjavik Study
note: A random population sample of Reykjavik residents born 1907-1935, examined from 1967 by the Icelandic Heart Association to prospectively study cardiovascular disease and its risk factors; a population study of one disease family, with no exposure basis.

label: Human Functional Genomics Project
note: A Nijmegen research programme collecting cohorts of healthy volunteers (500FG, 200FG, 300BCG) and some patient groups (obese, diabetic, HIV) to identify genetic and non-genetic determinants of immune and cytokine responses; its subject is immune variability, not one disease, and host factors such as season and vitamin D are studied as covariates rather than as an exposure design.

label: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III
note: An NHLBI transfusion-medicine research programme collecting blood donors and transfusion recipients (RBC-Omics donors, the Brazil sickle cell disease cohort and other protocols); its scope is blood safety and donor and recipient outcomes rather than one disease, and transfusion is a medical procedure, not an environmental exposure.

label: Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health
quote: The RPGEH was developed by the KPNC Division of Research as a resource that links together surveys, biospecimens and electronic health record data for research on the genetic and environmental determinants of common, age-related complex health conditions.
note: A Kaiser Permanente Northern California resource of consenting health-plan members (including the GERA adult cohort and a pregnancy cohort) linking surveys, biospecimens and records for common complex conditions; despite 'Environment' in its name, environmental determinants are one of many variables in a general resource, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Africa America Diabetes Mellitus Study
note: A genetic epidemiology study enrolling affected sib-pairs with type 2 diabetes and unaffected controls in Ghana, Nigeria and Kenya to map type 2 diabetes susceptibility genes; the affected sib-pairs make it a patient cohort, with no exposure basis.

label: Danish Blood Donor Study
note: A nationwide prospective cohort of healthy Danish blood donors with questionnaires, genotyping and registry linkage for research on donor health and public health in general; unselected healthy donors, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Howard University Family Study
note: A population-based family study of randomly ascertained African American families and unrelated individuals in Washington, DC, enrolled without selection on any phenotype to study common complex diseases (hypertension, obesity, type 2 diabetes) broadly; a general population sample with a broad purpose, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Stabilization of Atherosclerotic Plaque by Initiation of Darapladib Therapy Trial
note: An international randomized placebo-controlled trial of darapladib in 15,828 patients with stable coronary heart disease, whose baseline plasma biobank supports biomarker and genetic studies; a trial cohort of patients with one disease, and the only intervention is a drug.

label: Swedish BioFINDER Study
note: A prospective clinic-based cohort recruited 2009-2014 at neurology and memory clinics in southern Sweden, of patients with mild cognitive impairment, dementias and parkinsonian disorders alongside cognitively unimpaired older adults, to develop early diagnosis of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease; a patient cohort for neurodegenerative disease, with no exposure basis.

label: CROATIA-Vis Study
note: A population-based cohort of adults from the isolated island of Vis, Croatia, richly phenotyped for genetic studies of complex traits in an isolate; environmental exposures are measured among many phenotypes, so neither verdict is yes.

label: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center
note: The NIA-funded data resource pooling the standardized clinical, neuropathology and genetic data of participants of the US Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, which enrol people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment and controls for research on Alzheimer's disease and related dementias; an aggregation of disease-centre cohorts, with no exposure basis.

label: Singapore Prospective Study Program
quote: Individuals in these studies were sampled randomly from the Singapore population and a disproportionate sampling scheme was utilized to increase the sample sizes of Malays and Asian-Indians.
note: A population-based re-visit of adults randomly sampled for earlier Singapore surveys, stated to be a study of diabetes and cardiovascular disease; no exposure defines it or is its subject.

label: Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine Biobank
quote: We describe the biobank at the Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine (CCPM Biobank) that was jointly developed by the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus and UCHealth to serve as a unique, dual-purpose research and clinical resource accelerating personalized medicine.
note: An EHR-linked biobank of unselected adult UCHealth patients across all disease domains; neither an exposure nor a single disease defines it.

label: Adult Changes in Thought Study
quote: The study enrolls dementia-free persons aged 65 and older from the membership of Kaiser Permanente Washington [KPWA, previously Group Health Cooperative (GHC)] and follows them longitudinally.
note: A population-based cohort of dementia-free health-plan members aged 65 and over whose stated aim is risk and preventive factors for dementia; exposures are not its design purpose.

label: Hypertension Genetic Epidemiology Network
quote: HyperGEN recruited African American and White hypertensive sibships with 2 or more hypertensive sibs, at least 1 of them having severe HT.
note: A family study recruited through sibships with two or more hypertensive members (plus their offspring and population controls) to find genes for hypertension; no environmental exposure is involved.

label: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
quote: The design is a multicenter, two-armed, randomized trial with 37,000 females and 37,000 males in each of the two arms.
note: A randomised screening trial of about 155,000 men and women aged 55-74 not selected for disease, whose whole purpose is mortality from four cancers, so a population study of disease rather than a patient cohort; screening is a medical procedure, not an exposure.

label: Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II Biobank
quote: From 2004 to 2013, baseline data were collected from 156,701 individuals aged 20-85 years, recruited from 18 health promotion centers across Korea.
note: A population-based biobank of adults attending routine health examinations, established to study chronic diseases (cancer and cardiovascular disease) and their metabolic risk factors; despite the name, the purpose is broad chronic disease, so not a disease cohort, and no exposure defines it.

label: Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases-Heart Study
quote: All LIFE-Heart patients received diagnostic coronary angiography, and CAD was defined as at least one stenosis of ≥50% of any major coronary vessel.
note: A hospital-based biobank of patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected or confirmed coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction; no environmental exposure is involved.

label: Bandim Health Project
quote: Bandim Health Project (BHP) monitors health and survival of women and children in a nationally representative rural Health and Demographic Surveillance System (HDSS) in Guinea-Bissau.
note: A health and demographic surveillance system following the general population of women and children for child mortality, health interventions and vaccine effects; vaccines are medical interventions, not environmental exposures, and no disease defines it.

label: Center for Applied Genomics Biobank
quote: The cohort from the Center for Applied Genomics is composed of approximately 85,000 juvenile subjects below 18 years of age and of a diverse set of ancestries.
note: A paediatric hospital biobank recruiting children at CHOP with broad consent and EHR linkage, used for many childhood diseases (ADHD, atopic dermatitis and others); no single disease or exposure defines it.

label: Danish Twin Registry
quote: Because twins have been identified independent of traits and on a population basis, the Danish Twin Registry is well suited for studies to understand the influence of genetic and environmental factors for a wide variety of diseases and traits.
note: A nationwide twin register ascertained independent of traits; twin registries are neither exposure nor disease cohorts.

label: Electronic Medical Records and Genomics Network
quote: The Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE) Network, established in 2007, is a consortium of academic and integrated health systems conducting discovery and implementation research in translational genomics.
note: A consortium of EHR-linked biorepositories (BioVU, BioMe, MyCode, ACT and others) for genomic discovery and return of results across the phenome; its members are general biobanks, so no on both counts.

label: Sorbs Study
quote: All subjects are part of a sample from an extensively phenotyped isolated population from Eastern Germany, the Sorbs.
note: A volunteer sample of the Sorbs population isolate, phenotyped for metabolic and anthropometric quantitative traits; a general population cohort with no defining exposure or disease.

label: Dose-Responses to Exercise Training
exposures: regular physical exercise | healthy diet
quote: The Dose-Responses to Exercise Training (DR's EXTRA) study is a 4-y RCT on the health effects of regular physical exercise and a healthy diet in a population-based random sample of Finnish men and women aged 55–74 y living in the city of Kuopio in 2002 (see Supplemental Figure 1).
note: A randomised trial in a population-based random sample whose whole subject is the health effects of exercise and diet, so lifestyle exposures are its main subject (as assigned interventions rather than observed exposures, hence medium); participants were not selected for any disease.

label: Genetics of Lipid-Lowering Drugs and Diet Network
quote: As part of the NHLBI Programs in Gene by Environment Interaction (PROGENI), participants took part in diet and/or drug interventions (high-fat meal and/or fenofibrate for 3 weeks) and provided consent for genetic studies.
note: A family study of the genetics of lipid response to a single standardised high-fat meal challenge and three weeks of fenofibrate; the meal is a metabolic test and fenofibrate a medication, not environmental exposures, and families were not selected for disease. Borderline on exposure because of the gene-by-environment framing.

label: Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
quote: The Study of Women’s Health Across the Nation interviewed women in their 40s and 50s from seven U.S. cities approximately yearly to collect information on their physical, biological, psychological, and social health.
note: A community-based cohort of midlife women followed through the menopausal transition for health in ageing; menopause and ageing are not diseases and no exposure defines it.

label: Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study
quote: Finnish diabetic nephropathy study (FinnDiane) is an ongoing (1997->), nation-wide multicentre study focusing on diabetic complications and currently comprises of over 5000 adults with type 1 diabetes9,10.
note: A nationwide cohort of adults with type 1 diabetes followed for diabetic kidney disease and other complications; no environmental exposure is involved.

label: IMAGEN study
quote: Relevant to identifying gene-environment interactions on brain and behavior, the relatively homogeneous socioeconomic background of the Western European participating families meant IMAGEN was not well placed to investigate particular environmental influences such as nutrition or hazardous exposures.
note: Healthy 14-year-olds recruited from schools and followed for behavioural traits and their predictive value for frequent psychiatric disorders; the stated aim makes it a borderline population study of mental disorders. Its own authors say it was not placed to study environmental exposures.

label: Munich Antidepressant Response Signature
quote: MARS is a naturalistic open-label longitudinal treatment study with inpatients suffering from a depressive episode.
note: Inpatients admitted with a major depressive episode (unipolar or bipolar) followed during antidepressant treatment; antidepressants are medication, not an exposure.

label: Minority Aging Research Study
quote: MARS began in 2004 and recruited older African American individuals without known dementia.
note: A community-recruited cohort of older African Americans without dementia whose stated subject is cognitive decline and risk of Alzheimer's disease; no exposure defines it.

label: Older Australian Twins Study
quote: The Older Australian Twins Study (OATS) was recently initiated to investigate genetic and environmental factors and their associations and interactions in healthy brain ageing and ageing-related neurocognitive disorders.
note: A twin study of older Australians on healthy brain ageing as well as ageing-related neurocognitive disorders; a twin sample with a broad brain-ageing purpose, measuring occupational exposure only among many factors, so no on both counts.

label: LymeProspect
quote: The LymeProspect cohort consisted of 1138 patients with a new physician-confirmed LB (either EM or disseminated manifestation) who were included at the initiation of antibiotic therapy and followed for one year, between April 2015 and October 201818,19.
note: Patients with confirmed Lyme borreliosis followed after antibiotic treatment for persistent symptoms; defined by the infection as a disease, not by exposure to the agent.

label: 300-Tanzania-FG
quote: Briefly, the 300TZFG cohort consists of 323 healthy Tanzanian individuals aged between 18 and 65 years residing in the Kilimanjaro region in Northern Tanzania.
note: Healthy adult volunteers in northern Tanzania phenotyped for cytokine responses in a functional genomics project; environmental and dietary factors are analysed but do not define the cohort or its design.

label: UCLA ATLAS Community Health Initiative
quote: In this study, we investigate the role of genetic ancestry in a disease context within the UCLA ATLAS Community Health Initiative (or ATLAS for brevity), a biobank embedded within the UCLA Health medical system composed of de-identified, EHR-linked genomic data from a diverse patient population [17, 18].
note: An EHR-linked biobank of unselected UCLA Health patients used for phenome-wide studies; no exposure or single disease defines it.

label: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Family Study
quote: Recruitment for IRASFS was population-based and not based on disease status, e.g. diabetes.
note: Hispanic and African American families recruited on family size, not health status, to study the genetics of insulin resistance and visceral adiposity as quantitative intermediate phenotypes of type 2 diabetes and atherosclerosis; traits rather than a disease, and no exposure defines it.

label: WHI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network
quote: WHI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network – GARNET, which included all coronary heart disease, stroke, venous thromboembolic events and selected diabetes cases that happened during the active intervention phase in the WHI HT clinical trials and aged matched controls
note: A nested case-control GWAS sub-study of the WHI hormone therapy trials built from the coronary heart disease, stroke, venous thromboembolism and diabetes cases plus matched controls; hormone therapy is a medication, not an environmental exposure.

label: ALS Utrecht
note: Case-control sample of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis patients and healthy controls from UMC Utrecht contributed to the ENIGMA Plasticity meta-analysis; the cached texts hold only acknowledgements (Netherlands ALS Foundation) and the supplementary table is not downloaded, so the verdict rests on the definition only. No exposure defines it.

label: Brain Imaging Genetics study
quote: The Brain Imaging Genetics (BIG) study was initiated in 2007 and comprises healthy volunteer subjects, including many university students, who participate in diverse imaging studies at the Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging (DCCN), Nijmegen, The Netherlands (Franke et al., 2010).
note: Pool of self-reported healthy volunteers, mostly students, scanned at the Donders Centre for imaging genetics: no exposure or disease selection.

label: BrainSCALE study
quote: The participants were recruited from The Netherlands Twin Register (NTR) and at baseline consisted of 112 families, with 9-year-old twins and an older sibling.
note: Longitudinal twin-family study of normative brain development and cognition drawn from the Netherlands Twin Register; a twin registry sub-study about development, not exposure or disease.

label: Norwegian Cognitive NeuroGenetics sample
quote: Prominent features of the NCNG are the adult life-span coverage of healthy participants with high-dimensional imaging, and cognitive data from a genetically homogenous sample.
note: Healthy Norwegian adults across the life span collected for imaging and cognitive genetics; healthy-volunteer sample with no exposure or disease selection.

label: NeuroIMAGE study
note: Follow-up of the Dutch IMAGE ADHD families (probands with an ADHD diagnosis, their unaffected siblings) plus control families, designed to study the course of ADHD; environmental determinants are studied generically, so not an exposure cohort.

label: Inter99 Study
exposures: lifestyle | smoking cessation | physical activity/diet
quote: The aim of Inter99 is to assess the effect on IHD incidence of individually tailored non-pharmacological intervention on lifestyle using a newly developed computer-based health educational tool.
note: Population-based randomised trial of lifestyle counselling (smoking cessation, physical activity, diet) to prevent ischaemic heart disease in random samples of Copenhagen adults; lifestyle is its main subject, though as an intervention rather than an ambient exposure, so the exposure verdict is the debatable one.

label: iPSYCH case-cohort study
note: Danish population-based case-cohort sample of persons diagnosed with severe mental disorders plus a random population sub-cohort, built to study their genetic and environmental architecture; environment is generic, so not an exposure cohort.

label: Long Life Family Study
quote: The NIA Long Life Family Study (LLFS) is a longitudinal, multicenter, multinational, population-based multigenerational family study of the genetic and nongenetic determinants of exceptional longevity and healthy aging.
note: Families selected for exceptional familial longevity and healthy ageing; longevity is a trait, not a disease, and no exposure defines the cohort.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD
exposures: cigarette smoking (a history of ≥10 pack-year smoking)
quote: COPDGene enrolled 10,198 former and current smokers aged 45–80 years with a history of ≥10 pack-year smoking with and without COPD from initiation in P1 from 21 clinical centers across the United States (Figure 1) [4].
note: Multicentre cohort of current and former heavy smokers with and without COPD, ascertained on smoking status and COPD case-control status to find genetic factors and CT subtypes of COPD.

label: Genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors
note: Population-based cohort of healthy young adults in Liechtenstein whose stated purpose is the determinants of elevated blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors; counted as a population study of the cardiovascular disease family, though participants are free of cardiovascular disease at entry. Not an exposure cohort.

label: Women's Genome Health Study
quote: The Women’s Genome Health Study (WGHS) is a population-based, prospective cohort of initially healthy, female North American health care professionals at least 45 years old at baseline, representing participants in the Women’s Health Study (WHS) who provided a blood sample at baseline and consented for blood-based analyses.
note: Genome-wide subset of the Women's Health Study: initially healthy female health professionals followed for many incident outcomes (myocardial infarction, stroke, cancer, diabetes, osteoporosis); the health-professional sampling is a convenience population, not an occupational exposure, and the parent trial's aspirin and vitamin E are treatments.

label: Cameron County Hispanic Cohort
note: Community-based cohort of Mexican Americans in Brownsville, Texas, set up to determine the prevalence and determinants of obesity and diabetes; socio-economic status alone is not an exposure in scope.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium
note: US consortium assembling case-control, family-based and longitudinal Alzheimer disease cohorts (ADNI, NACC, ROS/MAP, MIRAGE and others) for genetic studies of late-onset Alzheimer disease; the smoking-interaction paper uses smoking as a covariate, not as the consortium's purpose.

label: Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America
quote: We estimated individual ancestry proportions in a sample of 7,342 subjects ascertained in five countries (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, México and Perú).
note: Admixed Latin American volunteers, mostly students and staff (soldiers in Chile), characterised for physical appearance and ancestry to study admixture and the genetics of physical traits; neither exposure nor disease selects them.

label: Mexico City Prospective Study
quote: MCPS is a prospective cohort of more than 150,000 adults, aged at least 35 years, who were recruited between 1998 and 2004 from the contiguous urban districts of Coyoacán and Iztapalapa in Mexico City23,55.
note: Large prospective general-population cohort of Mexico City adults followed for known and new risk factors for mortality; broad purpose, no exposure or disease selection.

label: Airwave Health Monitoring Study
exposures: use of TETRA, a digital communication system used by police forces and other emergency services in Great Britain | police work
quote: The Airwave Health Monitoring Study was established to evaluate possible health risks associated with use of TETRA, a digital communication system used by police forces and other emergency services in Great Britain since 2001.
note: Occupational cohort of police officers and staff across Great Britain, established to evaluate health risks of the TETRA digital radio (radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure, counted under radiation) and broadened to the health of the police workforce; not selected for any disease.

label: Cohorte Lausannoise
note: Random population sample of Lausanne adults whose stated purpose is the epidemiology and genetic determinants of cardiovascular risk factors and the metabolic syndrome, followed for incident cardiovascular events; counted as a population study of the cardiovascular disease family. Not an exposure cohort.

label: Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study
exposures: lifestyle
quote: The MCCS was initially carried out to study a wide range of research questions, primarily the link between lifestyle and the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases (Milne et al., 2017)
note: Prospective cohort of Melbourne adults recruited by Cancer Council Victoria primarily to study the link between lifestyle and the risk of cancer (and other chronic diseases); the cached text names only 'lifestyle', so the categories are the lifestyle exposures as a group, and cancer is the primary disease though the purpose extends to other chronic diseases.

label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey
note: Dutch population cohort of adolescents (plus a clinical cohort of child-psychiatric referrals) whose overall objective is the determinants of mental (ill-)health and social development, with psychiatric diagnostic interviews and psychiatric case-register linkage; counted as a population study of mental disorders. Not an exposure cohort.

label: ADDITION-PRO Study
note: Danish adults sampled from the high-risk strata of the ADDITION-Denmark stepwise diabetes screening programme (impaired glucose regulation, incident diabetes, lower-risk sub-sample) and followed for cardiovascular disease; selected for diabetes risk, not for an exposure.

label: Finnish Cardiovascular Study
note: Clinical cohort of patients scheduled for an exercise stress test at Tampere University Hospital, built to profile individuals at high risk of cardiovascular disease, events and death; many already have cardiovascular illness, so 'patients' would also fit. Not an exposure cohort.

label: Health Professionals Follow-up Study
note: Prospective cohort of US male health professionals with diet and lifestyle questionnaires every two to four years and many outcomes (erectile dysfunction, hearing problems, prostate and colorectal cancer); no cached text states whether nutrition was its design purpose, so the exposure question cannot be settled here (missing: the study's own statement of its aims). Outcomes are broad, so not a disease cohort.

label: ARGO study
note: Greek collection of patients with severe hip or knee osteoarthritis undergoing total joint replacement, with healthy controls, for osteoarthritis genetics; no exposure defines it.

label: Ansan and Ansung Study
quote: In the three population-based cohorts, 10,030, 173,357, and 28,338 participants were independently recruited from the KoGES_Ansan and Ansung study, the KoGES_health examinee (HEXA) study and the KoGES_cardiovascular disease association study (CAVAS), respectively.
note: Community-based population cohort of adults from Ansan and Ansung, the first KoGES cohort, studying common chronic diseases and their genetic and environmental risk factors; broad purpose, no exposure or disease selection.

label: Nagahama Prospective Cohort for Comprehensive Human Bioscience
quote: This study cohort was recruited from the general population living in Nagahama city, a largely rural city of 125,000 inhabitants in Shiga prefecture, located in the center of Japan.
note: General-population prospective cohort of Nagahama City residents for genomic and clinical research; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease Genetics Consortium
quote: Most studies included in CKDGen meta-analyses were population-based.
note: A GWAS meta-analysis consortium of mostly population-based studies dedicated to the genetics of kidney function and chronic kidney disease; its primary phenotype is eGFR, a quantitative trait, so the disease verdict rests on the consortium's stated purpose and name rather than on patient recruitment. No exposure design.

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Project
exposures: Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami
quote: The aims of TMM cohort studies are: 1) to monitor the effects of the damage caused by the GEJE on health status in the affected areas
note: Population-based adult and birth/three-generation cohorts of residents of the Miyagi and Iwate prefectures damaged by the 2011 earthquake and tsunami, launched to monitor the chronic health effects of the disaster; otherwise a general biobank with no single-disease focus.

label: Fred Hutchinson Prostate Cancer Study
note: Population-based case-control studies of prostate cancer in King County, Washington, with cases from the SEER registry and cancer-free controls; a disease cohort with no exposure design.

label: Whole Genome Association Analysis of Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT) Outcomes
note: Recipients of a first allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant for haematological malignancy or myelodysplasia at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, with their donors, genotyped for graft-versus-host disease and relapse; the transplant is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium
note: A meta-analysis consortium of mostly population cohorts studying quantitative glycaemic traits (fasting glucose, fasting insulin, 2-hour glucose, HbA1c) in individuals without diabetes; traits rather than a disease define its scope, so it is not recorded as a diabetes cohort, and nothing in its design concerns exposures.

label: Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Childhood Study
note: A UK pharmacogenetic study of adverse drug reactions in children whose cisplatin cohort is paediatric cancer patients phenotyped for hearing loss; chemotherapy is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Raine Study
quote: The Raine Study is a well-characterised pregnancy cohort located in Western Australia.
note: A Western Australian pregnancy cohort following mothers and offspring from gestation into adulthood to study early-life influences on later health and behaviour; a general birth cohort with no exposure or disease focus.

label: Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk
note: A statin trial in elderly people selected for pre-existing vascular disease or high risk of it, with coronary and stroke endpoints; part of the cohort are patients and the rest at risk, so the whole is recorded as at risk. Statin treatment is a medication, not an exposure.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt Sensitivity
exposures: dietary sodium | dietary potassium
quote: The objectives of the Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt Sensitivity (GenSalt) are to localize and identify genes related to blood pressure (BP) responses to dietary sodium and potassium intervention.
note: A family feeding study in rural China of blood pressure responses to controlled dietary sodium and potassium; diet is its main subject, though as an experimental intervention rather than an ambient exposure, hence medium confidence. Families were ascertained through probands with prehypertension or stage-1 hypertension, so probands and their relatives are at risk of hypertension.

label: Kaiser Permanente Research Bank
quote: The KP Research Bank (KPRB), a research resource within KP, is seeking to collect biospecimens and surveys from at least 400,000 adult members across the U.S. and linking that information to the EHR.
note: A health-system biobank of consenting adult Kaiser Permanente members linked to electronic health records, with general, pregnancy and cancer sub-cohorts; the resource as a whole is unselected by exposure or disease.

label: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
exposures: substance use
quote: The Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research (MCTFR) comprises multiple longitudinal, community-representative investigations of twin and adoptive families that focus on psychological adjustment, personality, cognitive ability and brain function, with a special emphasis on substance use and related psychopathology.
note: Community-representative twin and adoptive family studies whose special emphasis is substance use and related psychopathology (funded by NIAAA and NIDA, with one member study oversampled for risk of substance use disorders); substance use is a main subject, as in a smoking-behaviour consortium, and substance use disorders are a disease family, but the studies also cover personality, cognition and brain function broadly, hence medium confidence.

label: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease
note: Healthy European adults without diabetes, hypertension or dyslipidaemia, clamp-phenotyped and followed for atherosclerosis, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes; a healthy cohort, but one set up to study these specific diseases, so recorded as a population study of disease with medium confidence.

label: Rotterdam Study I
quote: The first cohort (RS-I) started in 1990 and included 7,983 inhabitants, aged ≥55 years from Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
note: The first cohort of the population-based Rotterdam Study, inhabitants aged 55 and over of a Rotterdam suburb, studying chronic diseases broadly; no exposure or single-disease design.

label: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
quote: With one important departure, the ABCD cohort recruitment emulates a multi-stage probability sample of eligible children: A nationally distributed set of 21 primary stage study sites, a probability sampling of schools within the defined catchment areas for each site, and recruitment of eligible children in each sample school.
note: A school-recruited probability sample of US children aged 9-10 followed for brain and cognitive development, mental health and substance use; the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue lists it for its geocoded linkage to air pollution and neighbourhood data, but exposures are one of many linked variables rather than the stated design purpose, and its outcomes are broad developmental ones.

label: Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
note: A pharmacogenetic challenge study of adults enriched for risk of type 2 diabetes given glipizide and metformin; the drug challenges are medication, not an exposure.

label: Colon Cancer Family Registry
note: An international registry of colorectal cancer cases (probands), their unaffected relatives and population controls; the probands are patients and the relatives at risk, so the registry is recorded under patients.

label: DIAbetes COhoRtE
note: A German prospective cohort of outpatients with prevalent type 2 diabetes followed for complications, chiefly renal events.

label: Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study
note: A community-based cohort of US men aged 65 and over designed to study risk factors for osteoporosis, fractures and prostate cancer, with a sleep ancillary study.

label: Prevention of Renal and Vascular End-stage Disease study
note: A Groningen general-population cohort, enriched for people with elevated urinary albumin plus a random sample, set up to study renal and cardiovascular disease as its name states; the albuminuria enrichment gives it an at-risk element.

label: European Alzheimer & Dementia Biobank
note: A European consortium pooling clinically diagnosed Alzheimer's disease case-control datasets for genetic studies of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.

label: INTERSTROKE Study
note: An international case-control study of first acute stroke; it quantifies modifiable risk factors including tobacco and alcohol, but the cohort is defined by disease and its risk-factor scope is broad rather than an exposure design.

label: Shanghai Women's Health Study
exposures: environmental exposures | lifestyle exposures
quote: The resources from the cohort will be valuable in future studies of environmental exposures and biomarkers for the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases.
note: A population-based cohort of Shanghai women set up, like other diet-and-cancer cohorts, to study environmental and lifestyle exposures (diet, soy, fish, tobacco, alcohol) and biomarkers in relation to cancer, with other chronic diseases secondary; exposure and cancer are both stated purposes.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank phase2
note: A nested case-control genotyping set of the Montreal Heart Institute Biobank: patients with coronary artery disease and CAD-free controls.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank phase1
note: The whole-genome-sequenced nested case-control set of the Montreal Heart Institute Biobank: patients with myocardial infarction and controls free of coronary artery disease.

label: Darmkrebs: Chancen der Verhütung durch Screening
note: A German population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer with active follow-up of the cases; a disease cohort with no exposure design.

label: British Genetics of Hypertension study
note: BRIGHT is a resource of affected sibling pairs and trios from severely hypertensive families, with normotensive controls, for the genetics of essential hypertension; participants were selected for the disease, not for any environmental exposure.

label: Genetic Investigation of ANthropometric Traits consortium
note: GIANT meta-analyses GWAS of anthropometric traits (height, BMI, waist measures) across population cohorts; its subject is body size and shape as quantitative traits, not a disease or an exposure, so it is no on both counts.

label: Hong Kong Degenerative Disc Disease Population Cohort
quote: Hong Kong Degenerative Disc Disease Population Cohort (HKDDDPC) is a a population-based cohort with subjects openly recruited via newspapers advertisement, posters and e-mails, regardless of their social and economic status
note: A population-based cohort of Southern Chinese volunteers recruited regardless of back symptoms and given lumbar MRI and genotyping so that intervertebral disc degeneration can be studied, hence a population study of one disease; environmental factors are only covariates.

label: International Lung Cancer Consortium
note: ILCCO pools lung cancer case-control and cohort studies (its members are lung cancer studies), so it is a disease aggregation of patients; tobacco is a risk factor it analyses, not the basis on which its studies were assembled.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project
note: ADSP sequences Alzheimer disease cases and controls drawn from many AD and population cohorts (its DSS page lists WES of 5,096 AD cases and 4,965 controls); an aggregation collected for one disease, with no exposure component.

label: Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey
exposures: early nutrition | infant feeding and life conditions
note: A community-based birth cohort of Cebu mothers and their 1983-84 infants followed on growth, schooling and health; the sources read describe recruitment and collection of environmental data but not the design purpose, so the exposure verdict (early nutrition as the cohort's subject) rests on the definition only; no disease focus.

label: HerediGene Population Study
note: A population genomics study enrolling any adult Intermountain Healthcare patient for whole-genome sequencing linked to health records; unselected for disease or exposure.

label: Heart and Vascular Health Study
note: A case-control study within Group Health of incident myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism and atrial fibrillation with a shared control group; the cases are patients with cardiovascular events, and there is no exposure basis.

label: Intermountain Heart Collaborative Study
note: A registry and biorepository of patients undergoing coronary angiography at Intermountain hospitals, followed for cardiovascular outcomes and used as an angiographic CAD case series (later widened as the INSPIRE registry); a clinical patient cohort, not an exposure cohort.

label: Johnston County Osteoarthritis Project
note: A population-based cohort of Johnston County adults sampled regardless of osteoarthritis status and followed for the incidence and progression of knee, hip and other osteoarthritis; one disease is its stated purpose, with no exposure basis.

label: London Life Sciences Prospective Population Study
note: A population-based cohort recruited from general practice lists to study the cardiometabolic risk of South Asians; a broad cardiometabolic purpose in a general population, so neither a disease nor an exposure cohort.

label: Asian Skin Traits and Genetics Research
note: A cohort of women from four Asian countries measured for 26 skin traits with genotyping and skin-related surveys; it studies normal trait variation, not a disease, and non-genetic factors are covariates rather than a design purpose.

label: Diet, Activity and Lifestyle Study
exposures: diet | physical activity | lifestyle
quote: Diet, physical activity, smoking, anthropometry, medical history, NSAID use, family history of cancer, demographics, race/ethnicity, and reproductive history data were obtained by questionnaire.
note: A population-based case-control study of colon and rectal cancer whose name and questionnaire centre on diet, physical activity and lifestyle as the risk factors under study; the cases make it a patient cohort and the design makes it a diet-and-cancer exposure study, though the sources read describe the data collected rather than stating the aim.

label: Invecchiare in Chianti
note: A population-based study of ageing sampled from municipal registries to study the loss of walking ability and other age-related decline; ageing and function are not diseases, and diet is measured only as a covariate.

label: Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Study
exposures: lifestyle factors in gene-environment interactions | alcohol consumption | smoking | food intake | exercise
quote: The Japan Multi-institutional Collaborative Cohort (J-MICC) study was launched in 2005 to examine gene-environment interactions in lifestyle-related diseases, including cancers, among the Japanese.
note: A Japanese population genome cohort whose stated purpose is gene-environment (lifestyle) interaction, with detailed alcohol, smoking, diet and exercise data, so lifestyle exposure is its design subject; its endpoints are cancer diagnosis and death, making it a population study of cancer, although the source frames this as lifestyle-related diseases mainly cancer.

label: Nijmegen Bladder Cancer Study
note: A case-control study of urinary bladder cancer patients identified through the Netherlands Cancer Registry, with population controls from the Nijmegen Biomedical Study; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Norwegian Breast Cancer Study
note: A Norwegian breast cancer case-control study within BCAC whose cases are incident breast cancers from three hospitals and whose tumour and normal breast tissue is used in expression studies; a patient cohort, no exposure basis.

label: QSkin Sun and Health Study
exposures: sun exposure and sunburns | use of tanning beds | sun protection behaviours
quote: At baseline, besides demographic items and general medical history, information about standard pigmentary characteristics (including hair and eye colour, freckling tendency, tanning ability and propensity to sunburn), past and recent history of sun exposure and sunburns, sun protection behaviours, use of tanning beds and history of skin cancer was collected by self-completed questionnaire.
note: A random population sample of Queensland adults established to study skin cancer and melanoma, with a baseline built around sun exposure, sunburn and tanning-bed history; a population study of one disease family whose design centres on ultraviolet exposure.

label: RIKEN Study
note: A Japanese knee osteoarthritis case-control collection of about 900 symptomatic cases diagnosed by orthopaedic surgeons and 3,400 controls, assembled for GWAS; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: RIKEN cohort
note: A pharmacogenetic series of metastatic renal cell carcinoma patients treated with sunitinib; a patient cohort, and treatment with a drug is not an environmental exposure.

label: Swedish Mammography Cohort
exposures: diet (food frequency questionnaire)
quote: The Swedish Mammography Cohort (SMC) [17] was established in 1987–1990 when 90,303 women born between 1914–48 and living in central Sweden (Uppsala or Västmanland counties) were invited to participate in a mammography screening program and to complete a food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) (74% response rate).
note: A population-based cohort of central Swedish women established around a food frequency questionnaire at mammography screening and followed through registers for diet, lifestyle and chronic disease; diet is its core design instrument, but its disease purpose is broad (chronic disease, notably cancer), so it is not a disease cohort.

label: Shanghai Men's Health Study
exposure categories: diet | tobacco | alcohol | physical activity | occupational
exposures: lifestyle/environmental factors | dietary habits | occupational history | physical activity
quote: The Shanghai Men's Health Study (SMHS) is a population-based cohort study of 61,480 men aged 40-74 years, launched in 2002 in urban Shanghai to investigate the contribution of lifestyle/environmental factors and genetic susceptibility to cancer and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs).
note: A population-based cohort of Shanghai men launched to investigate lifestyle/environmental factors (detailed diet, smoking, alcohol, occupation, physical activity) and genetic susceptibility, so exposure is its stated design purpose; its disease purpose (cancer and other non-communicable diseases) is broad, so not a disease cohort.

label: VITamins And Lifestyle Study
exposures: vitamin and mineral supplement use | diet | lifestyle
quote: Data were collected at baseline using a 24-page, self-administered, sex-specific, optically scanned questionnaire that covered three content areas: diet, supplement use, and health history and risk factors.
note: A prospective cohort of western Washington adults recruited within a SEER cancer-registry area with a baseline questionnaire on diet, supplement use and lifestyle, to study supplements and lifestyle in relation to cancer risk; the sources read show the design (supplement and diet content, cancer-registry catchment) but the cancer aim itself is stated only in the definition.

label: Western Australian Sleep Health Study
note: A clinic-based cohort of patients referred for sleep-disordered breathing to the sole public sleep clinic in Western Australia, phenotyped with polysomnography to study the genetics of obstructive sleep apnoea; a patient cohort with no exposure basis.

label: European Medical Information Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Multimodal Biomarker Discovery study
note: An aggregation of 11 European memory-clinic cohorts combined for Alzheimer disease biomarker discovery, spanning normal cognition, MCI and AD-type dementia with known amyloid status; assembled for one disease, no exposure basis.

label: NHLBI Family Heart Study
quote: The NHLBI Family Heart Study is a multicenter, population-based study of genetic and nongenetic determinants of coronary heart disease (CHD), atherosclerosis, and cardiovascular risk factors. In phase I, 2,000 randomly selected participants and 2,000 with family histories of CHD were identified among 14,592 middle-aged participants in epidemiologic studies.
note: NHLBI family study of the determinants of coronary heart disease: half the families were randomly sampled and half selected for high familial CHD risk from existing population studies, so it is a population study of one disease family (with an at-risk half) rather than a patient series; environments are mentioned only as generic determinants, not as a design focus.

label: Hyperglycemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcome Study
quote: The HAPO Study was an observational study designed to investigate the association between maternal glycemia during pregnancy, less severe than overt diabetes, and adverse pregnancy outcomes [34].
note: Multinational cohort of unselected pregnant women given a standard OGTT to relate maternal glycaemia below the diabetes threshold to pregnancy and newborn outcomes; participants were not selected for a disease and the stated subject is a glycaemia continuum and pregnancy outcomes rather than one disease (gestational diabetes was defined retrospectively in analyses), and no environmental exposure is studied.

label: Catheterization Genetics
quote: Individuals were selected from the CATHGEN biorepository of patients referred for evaluation of ischemic heart disease recruited sequentially through the cardiac catheterization laboratories at Duke University (Durham, NC) [30].
note: Clinical biorepository of patients recruited sequentially at cardiac catheterisation while being evaluated for ischaemic heart disease, followed for cardiovascular events; a patient series (the source also calls them patients at risk of heart disease, since not all prove to have CAD). No exposure defines it.

label: Colorectal Cancer Genetics & Genomics
quote: CRCGEN combines data of two Spanish case-control studies.
note: Spanish colorectal cancer case-control collection (incident CRC cases with hospital and population controls), used for colorectal cancer genetics; the cases are the cohort, controls included. No exposure focus.

label: Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Carlantino
quote: INGI-CAR - INGI-CARLANTINO INGI-CAR consisted of about 1000 subjects who were drawn from Carlantino, an isolated village of southern Italy.
note: Population-based genetic isolate cohort of an Apulian village, studied for complex traits in general (coffee consumption, sweet liking, ECG traits); neither an exposure nor a disease defines it.

label: EPIC-InterAct Study
exposures: diet | physical activity | lifestyle and behavioural factors
quote: This case-cohort study aims to investigate how genetic and potentially modifiable lifestyle and behavioural factors, particularly diet and physical activity, interact in their influence on the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
note: Case-cohort study nested in EPIC: all verified incident type 2 diabetes cases plus a random subcohort, assembled to study how diet and physical activity interact with genes in diabetes risk; the cases make it a disease cohort and the stated gene-lifestyle purpose makes it an exposure study.

label: Leipzig Adults
