note: A genomic subsample of the Mexican national household survey on tobacco, alcohol and drug use, assembled for addiction research: a population sample whose main subject is substance use, hence an exposure cohort and a population study of addiction.

label: Nicotine Addiction Genetics Finland study
exposures: ever-smoking | heavy smoking
quote: Twin pairs concordant for ever‐smoking were identified and recruited along with their family members (mainly siblings) for the Nicotine Addiction Genetics (NAG) Finland study.
note: Finnish twin pairs concordant for ever-smoking, enriched for heavy smokers, and their relatives, recruited to study nicotine dependence: smokers recruited as smokers, and at risk of nicotine addiction.

label: Netherlands Study of Cognition, Environment and Genes
quote: Participants volunteered in the Netherlands Study of Cognition, Environment and Genes (NESCOG), which comprises a general population sample (sample 1) and a genetically informative, family-based sample (sample 2).
note: A Dutch general-population and twin-family sample of volunteers studying individual differences in cognition; environmental factors are only questionnaire items and the disorder focus is broad, so neither verdict applies.

label: UK Nephropathy Family Study and Oxford Regional Prospective Study
note: A combined sample of two English cohorts of young people with childhood-onset type 1 diabetes, used for genetic studies of diabetic kidney disease; participants are patients.

label: Nephropathy Family Study
note: A longitudinal study of adolescents with type 1 diabetes and their parents, followed for the early pathogenesis of microalbuminuria; participants are patients, with no exposure focus.

label: Nigerian Breast Cancer Study
note: A breast cancer case-control study in Nigeria, later Cameroon and Uganda, whose cases are breast cancer patients; it studies general epidemiological and inherited risk factors without an exposure design focus.

label: National Joint Registry
note: A national registry of joint replacement procedures and implants; patients enter because of a surgical procedure, which is out of scope for exposure, and the registry is not defined by one disease, although diseased subsets (e.g. DDH) have been drawn from it.

label: National Psoriasis Victor Henschel BioBank
note: A National Psoriasis Foundation biobank of people with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis and unaffected controls, used as cases in case-control GWAS; no environmental exposure defines it.

label: National Survey of Physical Traits
note: A population-based cohort of Han Chinese volunteers studied for physical traits (face, ear, fingerprints) and multi-omics; traits are out of scope and no disease or exposure defines it.

label: New York Genome Center ALS Consortium
note: A consortium resource of blood and post-mortem tissue from ALS patients (with some other neurological disease and control donors); a disease cohort of patients.

label: NZ AAA Genetics Study
note: A New Zealand case-control study of abdominal aortic aneurysm; cases are AAA patients.

label: Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium
note: A consortium of pancreatic cancer case-control studies, so a disease aggregation of patients; it analyses smoking and alcohol among other risk factors, but no exposure defines the consortium or its members.

label: UPenn Local TGCT Study
note: A Philadelphia case-control study of genetic susceptibility to testicular germ cell tumour; cases are TGCT patients.

label: Phenotype, Genotype & Biomarkers in ALS and Related Disorders
note: A CReATe Consortium longitudinal observational study of patients with ALS and related disorders (and some family members).

label: PLATelet inhibition and patient Outcomes
note: A randomised trial of ticagrelor versus clopidogrel in patients with acute coronary syndrome; the only exposure is a medication, which is out of scope.

label: Pustular Psoriasis, Elucidating Underlying Mechanisms
note: A UK mechanistic study recruiting people with pustular psoriasis (with disease controls, healthy volunteers and relatives); smoking is studied as a risk factor but does not define the cohort.

label: Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics Study
note: A case-control genetic study of primary open-angle glaucoma in African Americans in Philadelphia; cases are glaucoma patients.

label: Project MinE
note: An international whole-genome sequencing consortium of ALS patients and matched controls; a disease aggregation of patients.

label: Pulmonary Hypertension and the Hypoxic Response in Sickle Cell Disease
note: A multicentre observational study of children and adolescents with sickle cell disease (with matched controls), designed to find predictors of pulmonary hypertension and other cardiopulmonary complications.

label: Queen Square Brain Bank for Neurological Disorders
note: A UK brain bank of donors with neurological, mostly neurodegenerative, diseases plus normal controls; a tissue bank of patients.

label: Genome-Wide Association Study on Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis in Quebec
note: A Quebec case-control study of calcific aortic valve stenosis in patients undergoing valve replacement, with surgical controls.

label: REDS-III Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort
note: A multi-centre Brazilian cohort of children and adults with sickle cell disease within REDS-III; transfusion is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Raine Eye Health Study
note: The 20-year eye follow-up of the Raine birth cohort, an unselected population sample whose stated purpose is one disease family, eye disease (with ocular biometry).

label: Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study
note: A hospital-based breast cancer case-control study in Philadelphia and Detroit, member of the ROOT consortium; cases are breast cancer patients.

label: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans
note: A population-based cross-sectional sample of Samoan adults whose stated purpose is genetic susceptibility to obesity and cardiometabolic phenotypes; diet and activity are measured but are not the design purpose.

label: Sanford Biobank
note: A hospital-based biobank of adult Sanford Health patients who volunteered specimens, not selected for a disease or exposure; used for studies such as coronary artery disease.

label: Salvador-SCAALA study
exposure categories: infection | air pollution | chemical | water | built environment | other
exposures: early life exposures of an urban population | intestinal helminth and parasitic infections | house-dust mite allergen and endotoxin | indoor and outdoor formaldehyde and particulate levels | urban sanitation
quote: Study designs used include surveys and case-control studies making possible the comparison of prevalence and risk factors for asthma and other allergic diseases between urban and rural environments (the Ecuador study) and a longitudinal study of the effects of early life exposures of an urban population on asthma and other allergic diseases (the Salvador study).
note: A cohort of children from poor areas of Salvador, originally enrolled to evaluate a sanitation programme, followed to study the effects of early-life environmental and infectious exposures on asthma and allergic diseases; its stated purpose is one disease family and its design centres on exposures.

label: San Francisco City Clinic Cohort
note: Homosexual and bisexual men recruited at a San Francisco STD clinic for studies of sexually transmitted hepatitis B, later followed for HIV infection and AIDS; they were selected as a high-risk group, and sexual behaviour is not an environmental exposure in scope.

label: Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial
note: A randomised trial of transfusion in children with sickle cell anaemia and silent cerebral infarcts; transfusion is a treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension
note: A Swiss family- and population-based study of randomly drawn adults and their relatives focused on the genetics of blood pressure and hypertension (and kidney function); environmental determinants are mentioned only alongside genetic ones.

label: SLOVENIA study
note: A clinical study of Slovenian children and young people with persistent asthma, studied for response to inhaled corticosteroids (a medication, out of scope as an exposure).

label: Santiago Longitudinal Study
exposures: nutrition | iron supplementation in infancy
quote: The SLS began September 1992 to study the effects of nutrition on children’s health, with follow-up assessments at ages 1, 5, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23, and 29 years.
note: A Chilean infancy cohort of healthy full-term infants recruited for an iron-supplementation trial, begun to study the effects of nutrition on children's health and listed in the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue; later follow-ups have broad aims (development, substance use, cardiometabolic risk), so it is not a disease cohort.

label: Shanghai Women's and Men's Health Studies
note: Two population-based prospective cohorts of middle-aged and elderly adults in urban Shanghai, analysed jointly; the bundle states no single disease or exposure as the design purpose, so no on both counts.

label: Swedish National Myeloma Biobank
note: National biobank of samples from multiple myeloma patients in Sweden; a patient biobank for one disease, no environmental exposure.

label: Seoul National University Hospital Diabetes Study
note: Case-control study of type 2 diabetes patients from the SNUH Diabetes Clinic with nondiabetic controls; disease cohort (cases), no exposure.

label: Hispanic Community Children's Health Study/Study of Latino Youth
note: Children of HCHS/SOL participants, not selected for disease or exposure; aims concern lifestyle behaviours and cardiometabolic risk factors in relation to acculturation and family factors, not a single disease or an environmental exposure.

label: Sao Paulo Heart Failure Cohort
note: Outpatients with symptomatic (stage C) heart failure at the São Paulo Heart Institute; patient cohort, no exposure.

label: Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes
exposures: nutrition prior to and during pregnancy | lifestyle | environmental factors assessed via household dust and skin samples
quote: The Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes (S-PRESTO) is a preconception, longitudinal cohort study that aims to study the effects of nutrition, lifestyle, and maternal mood prior to and during pregnancy on the epigenome of the offspring
note: Preconception mother-offspring cohort of women intending to conceive; its stated aim centres on preconception and pregnancy nutrition and lifestyle exposures and their effects on offspring, so exposure yes (diet); participants not selected for disease.

label: Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study
note: Nationwide cohort of children with blood culture-proven bacterial sepsis; defined by the disease (infection as illness, not exposure-uninfected), so disease yes, exposure no.

label: Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder
note: Multicentre treatment study of outpatients with bipolar disorder; patient cohort, and the only exposures are treatments.

label: Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination adjuvant treatment, as well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial
note: Randomised phase III adjuvant chemotherapy trial in patients with high-risk early breast cancer; trial of patients, exposure is only treatment.

label: Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for Renal Cell Carcinoma-Nephrectomy
note: Hospital registry of patients with renal cell carcinoma undergoing surgery; patient cohort, no environmental exposure focus.

label: Triple A Barcelona Study

note: Hospital-based hypertension case-control GWAS in Han Chinese in Shanghai.

label: Silk Road
quote: With the aim of studying the genetics of several phenotypes (e.g. food preferences, hearing and taste [9-12]), the Marco Polo scientific campaign, collected in 2010 genetic and phenotypic information of 411 individuals from six countries dwelling along the Silk Road (Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Tajikistan).
note: Isolated-population sample from communities along the Silk Road collected to study the genetics of senses and food preferences; neither disease nor exposure defines it.

label: Shanghai Jiao Tong University Diabetes Study
note: Type 2 diabetes case-control study at the Shanghai Diabetes Institute with early-onset familial cases and normoglycaemic controls.

label: Städtisches Klinikum Karlsruhe Deutsches Krebsforschungszentrum Study
note: Hospital-based breast cancer case series at Karlsruhe with GC-HBOC controls, a BCAC member study.

label: Singapore Translational and Clinical Research in Psychosis
note: National psychosis research programme in Singapore: schizophrenia patients for GWAS and a trial, plus an ultra-high-risk psychosis cohort; primarily patients.

label: Finnish Genetic Predisposition to Prostate Cancer Study
note: Population-based prostate cancer case-control study in Finland with registry-identified cases, a PRACTICAL member.

label: TASPRAC Study
note: Tasmanian prostate cancer resource combining a familial prostate cancer study and a population-based case-control study (PRACTICAL member); the quote names both components.

label: University of California San Francisco Atrial Fibrillation Study
note: Case set of atrial fibrillation patients from the UCSF electrophysiology laboratory, with early-onset cases sequenced in TOPMed.

label: University of Florida Diabetes Institute Study Bank
note: A type 1 diabetes study bank of patients, autoantibody-positive and other relatives, and controls; disease cohort (patients, with at-risk relatives), no environmental exposure focus.

label: Familial Prostate Cancer Study Ulm
note: A familial and sporadic prostate cancer case-control study in Ulm; cases are prostate cancer patients, no exposure focus.

label: University of North Carolina CanCORS study
note: The North Carolina CanCORS site: a population-based cohort of colorectal cancer patients; disease cohort, no exposure focus.

label: Utah Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Study
note: A CLL case-control GWAS in Utah with clinic and registry cases; disease cohort (patients), no exposure focus.

label: University of Wisconsin Transdisciplinary Tobacco Use Research Center Trial
exposures: cigarette smoking
quote: Study participants came from the Transdisciplinary Tobacco Use Research Centers (TTURCs) Study (1091 smokers of European descent), and the Genetically Informed Smoking Cessation Trial (GISC) Study (501 smokers of European descent).
note: A smoking cessation trial of adults smoking 10 or more cigarettes a day: participants were recruited as smokers (tobacco exposure) and treated for nicotine dependence, an addiction counted as a disease.

label: Västerbotten Intervention Project
quote: The VIP is an ongoing population-based cohort study initiated in 1985 in which all residents of Västerbotten County, Sweden, are invited to receive a health examination at ages 40, 50, and 60 with blood drawn for cryopreservation.
note: A population-based health-examination cohort of all Västerbotten residents at ages 40, 50 and 60; not selected for exposure, but set up as a programme against cardiovascular disease, so a population study of that disease family.

label: Wake Forest University Breast Cancer Study
note: A hospital-based breast cancer case-control study; disease cohort (patients), no exposure focus.

label: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial
exposures: low-fat eating pattern
quote: The CT is designed to allow randomized controlled evaluation of three distinct interventions: a low-fat eating pattern, hypothesized to prevent breast cancer and colorectal cancer and, secondarily, coronary heart disease;
note: The WHI randomised trials in unselected postmenopausal women; the dietary modification (low-fat diet) arm makes diet a design exposure, while the hormone and calcium/vitamin D arms are treatments; aimed at several diseases (CHD, breast and colorectal cancer, fractures), so not a single-disease cohort.

label: Weiss Laboratory Autism Collection
note: An aggregation of Californian autism case, trio and control collections genotyped for the PGC autism GWAS; disease (patients), no exposure focus.

label: Wenzhou Medical University Biobank - Tibetans
quote: The subjects were recruited at two separate sites (Seda and Litang) of the TP in Sichuan, western China
note: Tibetans recruited on the Tibetan Plateau for a study of genetic adaptation to high altitude; selection is by ancestry and residence for a genetic question, not an environmental hazard exposure, and no disease is targeted.

label: Washington University Genetics Study
note: A hospital-based case series of prostate cancer patients contributing to PRACTICAL; disease cohort, no exposure focus.

label: Nurses' Health Studies
quote: The NHS I began in 1976 when 121,700 female registered nurses, aged 30–55 years, were enrolled by completing a baseline questionnaire about their health and lifestyle [20].
note: An umbrella of the Nurses' Health Study cohorts: nurses enrolled as a general sample for risk factors of major chronic diseases, not selected for an occupational hazard and not about one disease.

label: International Consortium on the Genetics of Heroin Dependence
note: A heroin dependence case-control genetics consortium; cases have the addiction (a disease); illicit drug use is not among the exposure categories here, so exposure is no.

label: Cardiovascular Effects of Air Pollution and Noise in Stockholm
exposures: ambient air pollution | noise
quote: Recruiting individuals from Stockholm County the Cardiovascular Effects of Air pollution and Noise Study (CEANS) cohort was included.
note: Four Stockholm population cohorts pooled to study air pollution and noise as risk factors for cardiovascular disease; the study name itself states both the exposures and the disease.

label: My Purchases cohort
exposures: diet from consumer purchases | household lifestyle exposures | household chemicals
quote: This project aims to investigate how what we buy, and thus our diet, affects health, by analyzing purchase patterns and health information over time.
note: A Danish cohort donating digital purchase receipts to study how diet and household lifestyle exposures affect health; open to all adult residents, not about one disease.

label: Study on Transitions in Employment, Ability and Motivation
exposures: work characteristics
quote: From the inception of the cohort in 2010 (T1) onwards, participants completed an online questionnaire on topics such as work characteristics, health, employment status and transitions, work ability, and work productivity.
note: A Dutch occupational-health cohort of people aged 45-64 on work characteristics, health and work participation, part of the OMega-X occupational exposome consortium; counted as designed around occupational exposures, though its main outcome is work participation rather than exposure effects, so the exposure verdict is borderline.

label: Swedish Cervical Screening Cohort
quote: The CSC contains stored cervical cells from almost the entire screening population of women in the capital region of Stockholm, Sweden.
note: The Stockholm cervical screening population with biobanked cervical samples, run by a cervical cancer elimination centre; a population study of cervical cancer. HPV is screened for as the disease cause, not as a defining exposure; the cohort is also used by the HEAP exposome project, but exposure is not its design basis.

label: Dutch Famine Birth Cohort
exposures: acute maternal undernutrition during the 1944-1945 Dutch famine | prenatal famine exposure
quote: The cohort was set up to investigate the effects of acute maternal undernutrition during specific stages of gestation on the offspring’s adult health.
note: A famine-exposed birth cohort born around the Dutch Hunger Winter, set up to study prenatal undernutrition; outcomes span cardiovascular, metabolic, ageing and mental health, so not a single-disease cohort.

label: Diabetes Prediction in Skåne
note: Newborns in Skåne screened for type 1 diabetes risk, with at-risk children followed for islet autoantibodies; at-risk disease cohort. Environmental triggers are mentioned only in the definition, not as a stated design centre in the sources read.

label: Étude Longitudinale Française depuis l'Enfance
exposures: emerging exogenous pollutants | environmental contaminants
quote: The priority research themes selected for ELFE were:aspects of children's environment that have undergone the most striking changes over recent decades including: modification of nutritional intake; reduction of physical activity; exposure to emerging exogenous pollutants;
note: The French national birth cohort, formed by merging a social-science project with an environmental-health project on pollutant exposure of pregnant women and children; exposure to emerging pollutants is a priority theme, though the cohort's objective is broad; not a disease cohort.

label: ENVIRonmental influence ON early AGEing
exposures: early-life environmental exposures | air pollution | green space
quote: Within the ongoing population-based prospective birth cohort study ENVIRONAGE we explore new dimensions in the current understanding of human ageing and its interaction with the environment
note: A population-based Belgian birth cohort built to study how early-life environmental exposures (air pollution named on the study website, green space in its papers) influence ageing; ageing is not a disease.

label: Finnish HPV vaccination cohort
note: A community-randomised HPV vaccination trial of unselected Finnish adolescents followed for HPV; the intervention is a vaccine (a medical procedure, not an environmental exposure), and the trial's single disease focus is HPV infection.

label: Nascita e INFanzia: gli Effetti dell'Ambiente
exposures: early life exposures | pre-natal and early post-natal exposures
quote: The NINFEA cohort is an Internet-based birth cohort established in Italy with the aim of investigating the effects of early life exposures on the health of newborns, infants, adolescents and adults.
note: An Italian internet-recruited birth cohort named for and set up to study the effects of the environment and early-life exposures; not about one disease.

label: Rhea Study
exposures: Mediterranean diet
quote: The uniqueness of this cohort is that it takes place in the island of Crete where the beneficial effect of the Mediterranean diet was first described during the Seven Countries Study of Cardiovascular Diseases, started at the end of the 1950s.
note: A population-based mother-child cohort in Crete created in response to childhood obesity, set in the context of the changing Mediterranean diet; the obesity focus is stated directly, the diet-exposure design is indirect (it is also used for prenatal metal exposure studies).

label: Rotterdam Study III
quote: RS-III-1 refers to the baseline examination of all persons aged 45 years and over living in the study district that had not been examined already (i.e., mainly comprising those aged 45–60 years).
note: The third Rotterdam Study cohort of all residents aged 45 and over in the district, studying chronic diseases broadly; neither exposure- nor single-disease-based.

label: Suivi de l'Exposition à la Pollution Atmosphérique durant la Grossesse et Effets sur la Santé
exposures: air pollution exposure during pregnancy | phthalates and DINCH | non-persistent endocrine disruptors
quote: (1) characterize finely environmental exposures during pregnancy and early life ; (2) evaluate the impact of the environment on mother-child health, focusing on three main outcomes: growth, respiratory health and neurodevelopment
note: SEPAGES is a Grenoble couple-child cohort whose name and stated aims centre on characterising environmental exposures (air pollution, endocrine disruptors) in pregnancy and early life; it is a population birth cohort, not a disease cohort.

label: Sysdimet study
exposures: a diet high in fatty fish, bilberries and wholegrain products | whole-grain-enriched diet
quote: We evaluated whether a diet high in fatty fish, bilberries and wholegrain products (Healthy Diet) improves biomarkers reflecting inflammation and endothelial dysfunction in individuals with impaired glucose metabolism.
note: Sysdimet is a 12-week dietary intervention trial whose main subject is diet; participants were selected for impaired glucose metabolism and metabolic syndrome features, a pre-disease state for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

label: Finnish Maternity Cohort
note: The FMC is a nationwide biobank of leftover first-trimester sera from essentially all pregnant women in Finland, i.e. unselected donors; it is used mainly for cancer studies via registry linkage but was not recruited for a disease or an exposure.

label: Polish-Norwegian Study
quote: The recruitment into PONS study was based on a broad media campaign.
note: PONS is a community-based cohort of volunteers aged 45-64 from the Kielce region studying health, lifestyle behaviours and chronic disease risk factors broadly; neither one exposure nor one disease defines it.

label: Monitoring Project on Risk Factors for Chronic Diseases
note: MORGEN is a Dutch random population sample aged 20-65 in which risk factors for chronic diseases (cardiovascular and others) were monitored; its purpose is broad chronic disease rather than one disease, and no exposure defines it.

label: Generation R Next Study
note: Generation R Next is a population-based Rotterdam preconception and pregnancy cohort about growth, development and health of children and parents; not exposure- or disease-defined.

label: Nordic Children and Adults Born Preterm
note: NORDCAP is a register-based total birth cohort of all births in Finland, set up to study how preterm birth and pregnancy disorders predict later outcomes; participants are unselected and environmental exposures are only one later-added theme.

label: Wearable data collection study
exposures: exposome estimated from blood, saliva, sweat and personal aerosols | multiple exposures monitored with wearable exposure sensors
quote: Longitudinal cohort of pregnant and non-pregnant women for exposome estimation from blood, saliva, sweat and personal aerosols.
note: The HEAP wearable data collection study is an exposome pilot following pregnant and non-pregnant women with personal exposure monitors; its purpose is exposure measurement, and participants are not selected for disease.

label: Kardiovize Brno 2030
quote: We randomly selected a 1% sample of the city of Brno residents aged 25-64 years stratified by sex and age.
note: Kardiovize Brno 2030 is a random population sample of Brno residents designed as a cardiovascular health study; environmental factors are one of many measured domains.

label: 1970 British Cohort Study
note: BCS70 is a national birth cohort of people born in one week of 1970 followed for health, development and social circumstances; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: Study on the influence of Air pollution on Lung function, Inflammation and Ageing
exposures: air pollution exposure | long-term exposure to particulate matter and NO2 from traffic and industry
quote: The SALIA study was initiated in the early 1980s by the State Government of North-Rhine Westphalia to investigate the health effects of air pollution exposure in women.
note: SALIA is a population-based cohort of women from the industrial Ruhr Area and rural comparison areas, set up to study the health effects of air pollution; participants were not selected for disease.

label: NoMa study
exposures: replacing saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat in commercial food items
quote: This randomized controlled trial aimed to investigate the health effects of replacing food items with a high content of saturated fatty acids with food items where a large portion of the saturated fat had been replaced with polyunsaturated fat.
note: NoMa is an 8-week dietary fat-quality intervention trial whose main subject is diet; participants were otherwise healthy adults recruited for moderate hypercholesterolemia.

label: National Health and Nutrition Survey – HYDRIA
exposures: dietary intake | adherence to the Mediterranean diet
quote: The study design for the HYDRIA survey followed the recommendations of the European Health Examination Survey (EHES) [18] and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) [19] for the collection of health and dietary data at a national level, allowing for intercountry comparisons.
note: HYDRIA is a nationally representative Greek health examination and nutrition survey whose design centres on measuring dietary intake (EFSA methodology) alongside health; participants are a population sample, not a disease group.

label: Grain Fibre Modification for Gut-mediated Health Effects
exposures: wholegrain rye bread | wheat bread enriched with bioprocessed rye bran
quote: The aim was to investigate whether the white wheat bread enriched with bioprocessed rye bran (BRB + WW) promotes similar effects to WGR on glucose metabolism and plasma levels of SCFAs in healthy subjects with self-reported gastrointestinal symptoms.
note: FIBREFECTS is a crossover cereal-fibre intervention trial whose main subject is diet; participants were healthy adults with self-reported gastrointestinal symptoms (a symptom, not a diagnosed disease; IBD and coeliac disease were exclusions).

label: Piccolipiù birth cohort
quote: Piccolipiù is a multipurpose birth cohort set up in multiple sites, in central and northern Italy.
note: Piccolipiù is a multipurpose Italian birth cohort of unselected newborns; environmental exposures are one of several stated aims beside parental conditions and social factors, and most planned questions concern maternal and social risk factors, so it is not an exposure cohort (borderline).

label: Foods for weight management
exposures: satiety value of foods in a weight-maintenance diet | very-low-energy diet
quote: This study aimed to investigate factors associated with weight management, especially whether satiety value of food as a part of a weight-maintenance diet would affect self-regulation of food intake and weight management.
note: ELIPA is a weight-management dietary trial in obese adults comparing foods of higher and lower satiety value; diet is its main subject and obesity is the recruitment criterion.

label: Constances
quote: It was designed as a general-purpose prospective cohort intended to serve as an open epidemiological research infrastructure accessible to the scientific community for conducting ancillary projects on a variety of research questions.
note: CONSTANCES is a general-purpose French population cohort drawn from national health insurance beneficiaries; it has a declared focus on occupational and social factors among other areas, but occupational exposure does not define it, and its disease interests are broad (chronic diseases, ageing).

label: Gene and Environment: Prospective Study on Infancy in Italy
note: GASPII is a Rome birth cohort piloting a national Italian birth cohort to study genetic and environmental influences on child health in general; its members are unselected newborns and no single exposure or disease defines it.

label: Kaunas cohort
exposures: drinking water disinfection by-products during pregnancy | early-life exposome (HELIX)
quote: Concentrations of drinking water disinfection by-products (DBPs) during pregnancy were estimated from water company concentration and distribution data as part of the water contaminants and stillbirth, congenital anomalies, birth weight, preterm delivery (HiWate) project in four of the cohorts (BiB, KANC, INMA, RHEA).
note: KANC was set up as the Kaunas cohort of the EU HiWATE project on drinking-water contaminants and pregnancy outcomes and later joined the HELIX exposome project; all pregnant women in Kaunas were invited, so it is not disease-selected.

label: Central European Longitudinal Studies of Parents and Children: Young Adults
note: CELSPAC: YA is a population-based follow-up of the young adults of the Czech ELSPAC birth cohort plus peers, siblings and partners, studying lifestyle, social and environmental factors and early signs of chronic disease broadly.

label: European Longitudinal Study of Pregnancy and Childhood
note: ELSPAC-CZ is a population-based birth cohort of children born in Brno and Znojmo in 1991-1992, with broad aims covering biological, psychosocial, economic and environmental factors on child development.

label: Perturbateurs Endocriniens: Étude Longitudinale sur les Anomalies de la Grossesse, l’Infertilité et l’Enfance
exposures: prenatal exposure to environmental and occupational chemicals | pesticides (triazine and chloroacetanilide herbicides) | endocrine disruptors
quote: The PELAGIE mother-child cohort was set up with the aim to study the effect of prenatal exposure to environmental and occupational chemicals on reproduction and child development.
note: PELAGIE is a Brittany mother-child cohort set up to study prenatal exposure to environmental and occupational chemicals such as pesticides and endocrine disruptors; participants are pregnant women from the general population.

label: Generation XXI
note: Generation XXI is a population-based Porto birth cohort studying early-life determinants of growth and health in general; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: Moli-sani Study
note: Moli-sani is a random population sample of adults in Molise studying genetic and environmental risk factors for chronic-degenerative diseases (cardiovascular, cancer, neurodegenerative) broadly; no single disease or exposure defines it.

label: Central European Longitudinal Studies of Parents and Children: The Next Generation
exposures: exposome factors (environment, lifestyle, nutrition) in pregnancy and early childhood
quote: This prospective birth cohort is designed to follow up 7000 children from their prenatal period to adolescence with the aim of assessing EXPOSOME factors potentially affecting children health.
note: CELSPAC: TNG is a Brno birth cohort run by RECETOX whose stated aim is assessing exposome factors affecting child health; it enrols unselected pregnant women and looks at chronic diseases and developmental disorders broadly.

label: Cypriot Children's Health and Environment Observatory
exposures: children's exposome (molecular biomarkers, sensors and questionnaires across the three exposome domains)
quote: The CHILDREN_FIRST international cohort observatory study aims to investigate how the spatio-temporal evolution of the children’s exposome profiles in the Mediterranean region influences early-life programming of chronic disease risk during the critical window of susceptibility in primary school years (6–11 years of age).
note: Cypriot site of an exposome-based children's cohort built around the exposome; participants are unselected first-grade schoolchildren and the disease aim is broad (chronic disease risk).

label: Observation of Cardiovascular Risks and Health in Luxembourg
note: Nationwide population-based survey whose stated purpose is cardiovascular risk factors, so a population study of cardiovascular disease; lifestyle and greenness are measured but exposure is not the design purpose.

label: Barcelona Life Study Cohort
exposures: socio-environmental exposome during pregnancy and childhood
quote: The Barcelona Life Study Cohort (BiSC) is an exposome cohort, aiming to comprehensively evaluate the socio-environmental and genetic determinants (i) of foetal and child health, growth, and development towards adult life and (ii) of maternal mental and physical health and wellbeing during pregnancy and afterwards, while shedding light on the underlying biological mechanisms.
note: Exposome birth cohort of general-population pregnant women in Barcelona; designed around exposures, not selected for any disease.

label: Puberty and metabolic risk in obese children. Epigenetic alterations and pathophysiological and diagnostic implications
note: Pubertal follow-up of GENOBOX children (a childhood-obesity case-control study) grouped by obesity and insulin resistance to study metabolic syndrome progression; no environmental exposure focus.

label: Study of Secondary Exposure to Pesticides among Children, Adolescents, and Adults
exposures: secondary (take-home and residential) pesticide exposure in a floricultural community | agrochemicals | PFAS, PCBs, PBDEs, DEET
quote: ESPINA is a prospective cohort established in 2008 that aims to investigate the impacts of pesticide exposure on development from childhood to adulthood in individuals living within the agricultural community of Pedro Moncayo, Pichincha, Ecuador.
note: Children of an agricultural community in Ecuador, recruited with a balance of those living and not living with floricultural or agricultural workers, followed for pesticide effects; not a disease cohort.

label: Rome Longitudinal Study
note: Administrative census-based cohort of all Rome residents; air pollution, noise and greenness are linked to addresses and used in later analyses, but no source states exposure as its design purpose.

label: Prevention Cube
exposures: occupational exposures across employment sectors
quote: To build a 'data warehouse' to make OHS data available for research and to investigate sector-specific health problems.
note: Occupational health surveillance records of Belgian employees pooled for research on work-related and sector-specific health problems (a member of the OMega-X occupational exposome consortium); no single disease.

label: Czech Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe study
exposures: alcohol | nutrition
quote: The main hypotheses of the HAPIEE study relate to the role of alcohol, nutrition and psychosocial factors.
note: Czech arm of HAPIEE, a population-register random sample whose main hypotheses concern alcohol and nutrition; its disease aim covers cardiovascular and other non-communicable diseases, too broad for a disease cohort.

label: International Lipid-Based Nutrient Supplements Project-DYAD-Malawi
exposures: small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements | multiple micronutrients | iron-folic acid
quote: A Research Plan for a Randomised, Single-blind, Parallel Group Controlled Trial in Rural Malawi, Testing the Health Effects of Supplementing Maternal Diet During Pregnancy and Lactation and Infant Diet From 6 to 18 Months of Age With High-energy, Micronutrient Fortified Lipid-based Nutrient Supplements (LNS)
note: Randomised trial of maternal and infant dietary supplementation in rural Malawi; diet is its main subject (borderline, as the supplements are partly micronutrient capsules), and participants had uncomplicated pregnancies.

label: New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study
exposures: arsenic from private well water | environmental contaminants
quote: The New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study is a research project that is investigating how various factors such as contaminants in the environment affect the health of pregnant women and their children.
note: Birth cohort built to study environmental contaminants such as arsenic in private well water; pregnant women recruited at prenatal clinics without disease selection.

label: Shanghai Dapuqiao Aging and Cognition Study
note: Community-based cohort of older Shanghai residents recruited through the annual physical examination programme to study health, lifestyle and cognition in ageing; no disease or exposure selection.

label: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe
note: Population-based multidisciplinary panel survey of people aged 50 and over on health, ageing and socio-economics; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: Harmonized Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India
note: Population-representative study of late-life cognition and dementia, oversampling people at high risk of cognitive impairment; environmental exposures are collected only as one set of dementia risk factors.

label: Hokkaido Study on Environment and Children's Health
exposures: low-level environmental chemical exposures | PFAS | tobacco smoke
quote: Our primary objectives are to (1) examine the effects that low-level environmental chemical exposures have on birth outcomes, including birth defects and growth retardation;
note: Birth cohort designed to study prenatal and postnatal environmental chemical exposures; outcomes span birth defects, growth, allergies, infections and neurodevelopment, so no single disease.

label: GINIplus/LISA North
exposures: infant nutritional intervention | environmental and lifestyle influences on allergy development
quote: The GINIplus (German Infant Nutritional Intervention plus environmental and genetic influences on allergy development) and LISA (Influence of Lifestyle factors on the development of the Immune System and Allergies) studies are prospective population-based birth cohorts from East and West Germany.
note: Pooled Wesel (rural, near the Ruhr) participants of two population-based German birth cohorts whose stated purposes are nutritional, environmental and lifestyle influences on allergy development; used in the ESCAPE air-pollution analyses.

label: Walnuts Smart Snack Dietary Intervention Trial
exposures: walnut intake (omega-3 fatty acids)
quote: a randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate whether dietary supplementation with four walnuts per day (30 kernel grams) for 6 months improved brain neuropsychological and socio-emotional development compared to a control group (abstention from walnuts) in healthy teenagers (11–16 years old)
note: School-based randomised dietary intervention trial (walnuts) in healthy adolescents; diet is its main subject, and participants are healthy.

label: GENOBOX study
note: Hospital-based case-control study of children with overweight or obesity and controls, set up to study childhood obesity; diet and activity are analysed but exposure is not the design.

label: Rio Birth Cohort Study on Environmental Exposure and Childhood Development
exposures: environmental chemical pollutants | metals | pesticides | plasticizers
quote: The Rio Birth Cohort Study (PIPA project) is a prospective maternal-infant health study, hosted in the city of Rio de Janeiro (Southeastern Brazil), designed to investigate separate and combined effects of environmental chemical pollutants, as well as the interactions between these exposures and sociocultural environment and epigenetic patterns.
note: Hospital-based birth cohort designed to study prenatal and early-life exposure to metals, pesticides and plasticisers; all births at one maternity hospital, no disease selection.

label: Programming Research in Obesity, Growth, Environment and Social Stressors
exposures: metals | air pollution | phthalates
quote: PROGRESS is a longitudinal birth cohort study conducted in Mexico that investigates prenatal exposure to mixtures of metals, air pollution, and phthalates.
note: Mexico City birth cohort built around prenatal metals, air pollution and phthalates; outcomes are neurodevelopment, growth and metabolic health broadly, so not a disease cohort despite 'obesity' in the name.

label: Infants' Environmental Health Study
exposures: prenatal pesticide exposure (aerially sprayed mancozeb, ETU) | manganese
quote: The Infants’ Environmental Health Study [Infantes y Salud Ambiental (ISA)] is a prospective community-based birth cohort study in Matina County, Limón, Costa Rica, aimed at examining possible effects of prenatal pesticide and manganese exposure on children’s growth and neurodevelopment.
note: Birth cohort of pregnant women living near banana plantations with aerial mancozeb spraying, designed to study pesticide and manganese exposure; not disease-selected.

label: Multi-Partner Consortium to Expand Dementia Research in Latin America
note: Multicentre cohort of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia patients with controls; its 'exposome' is chiefly social vulnerability and socio-economic indicators, which is not an environmental exposure design.

label: Sustainable plant protection transition: a global health approach
exposures: pesticide mixtures (plant protection products) among farmers, neighbours of agricultural fields and consumers
quote: Cross-sectional study performed in 2021 to assess differences in exposure of farmers (organic and non-organic practises), neighbours (people living close to agricultural fields) and controls ('consumers' living away from agricultural fields) to pesticides.
note: Field study recruiting farmers, neighbours of fields and distant consumers by expected pesticide exposure for biomonitoring and risk assessment; no disease selection.

label: Maule Cohort
note: Population-based census cohort of an agricultural county studying the natural history of chronic diseases broadly; pesticides and pollutants are among many risk factors, not the design purpose.

label: Survey on Health, Well-Being, and Aging in Colombia
note: Population-based national survey of community-dwelling older Colombians on health, ageing and social determinants; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: Encuesta Nacional de Situación Nutricional
exposures: dietary intake | nutritional situation
quote: The ENSIN-2015 estimated dietary intake using the 24-hour recall method (24 HR) [13, 14].
note: Nationally representative national nutrition survey whose main subject is the population's diet and nutritional situation; not selected for any disease.

label: Cohorts Consortium of Latin America and the Caribbean
quote: Data sources were included in the CC-LAC database if they had at least a baseline and one follow-up round, included LAC populations living in LAC, and participants were not recruited exclusively based on the presence of a risk factor or disease.
note: Consortium pooling population-based Latin American and Caribbean cohorts (not recruited for a risk factor or disease) to study cardio-metabolic risk factors and cardiovascular outcomes; a population study of cardiovascular disease, not an exposure consortium.

label: Ecuador Life
exposures: soil-transmitted helminth (STH) parasites | early-life microbial exposures
quote: The ECUAVIDA birth cohort is studying the impact of exposures to soil-transmitted helminth (STH) parasites and early-life microbial exposures on the development of atopy, allergic diseases and immune responses in childhood.
note: Rural Ecuadorian birth cohort designed around early-life helminth and microbial exposures, with allergic disease, atopy and asthma as its stated outcomes.

label: Banco Nacional de Tumores Terry Fox
note: National tumour bank of the Colombian cancer institute: donors with cancer (tumour tissue), cancer survivors and donors without cancer; a cancer patient biobank. Risk-factor questionnaires are routine, not an exposure design.

label: China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study
quote: The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) is a nationally representative longitudinal survey of persons in China 45 years of age or older and their spouses, including assessments of social, economic, and health circumstances of community-residents.
note: Nationally representative ageing survey of Chinese adults aged 45+; general population, neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: REal-time Assessment of Community Transmission
quote: The study team (researchers from Imperial College London and its logistics partner Ipsos) wrote to named individuals aged 5 years and older in random cross-sections of the population of England, using the National Health Service list of patients registered with a general practitioner (near-universal coverage) as a sampling frame.
note: Random population samples of England tested for SARS-CoV-2 infection and antibodies, now a recontactable cohort; a population study of COVID-19, not an environmental exposure cohort.

label: 3xG study
exposures: environmental exposures via biomonitoring | environmental and lifestyle exposure
quote: The aim of the 3xG study is to follow-up the health and development of growing children as a sentinel population and to study the influence of environmental exposures via biomonitoring.
note: Local Flemish birth cohort in the nuclear-waste municipalities Dessel, Mol and Retie built around human biomonitoring of environmental exposures (metals, PFAS, glyphosate measured); general health follow-up, no disease focus.

label: Cohort ’18, Growing Up in Hungary
quote: It is based on a nationwide representative sample of pregnant women who gave birth between March 2018 and April 2019.
note: Nationally representative Hungarian birth cohort on childbearing, childrearing and child development; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: COMmunity-based Behavior and Attitude survey in Tuvalu
exposures: food consumption patterns | lifestyle behaviors | climate change
quote: The COMBAT cohort is a longitudinal, community-based study in Tuvalu examining lifestyle behaviors, environmental exposures, and health outcomes.
note: Nationwide community survey/cohort of Tuvaluan adults centred on diet, lifestyle behaviours and climate-related exposures; outcomes are obesity and non-communicable diseases broadly, so not a single-disease cohort.

label: São Paulo Western Region Birth Cohort
quote: The primary objective of the ROC study is to assess the impact of social and environmental factors on early childhood development in the modern urban low-income setting of São Paulo.
note: Birth cohort of all local births at one São Paulo hospital studying social factors and toxic stress on child development; the named exposures are psychosocial (toxic stress, neighbourhood violence), not an in-scope environmental agent, and there is no disease focus.

label: Next Steps
quote: Next Steps (previously known as the Longitudinal Study of Young People in England, LSYPE) is an ongoing, multidisciplinary, longitudinal study following 16 122 people who were in secondary school in England and were born in 1989–90.
note: National school-based cohort of young people in England born 1989-90, multidisciplinary; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: PROMESA cohort study
exposures: particulate matter (PM2.5) | NO2 | external exposome (ambient and indoor exposures)
quote: This study aims to characterize the external exposome (ambient and indoor exposures) and its contribution to clinical respiratory and early biological effects in children.
note: Randomly sampled under-five children in high and low PM2.5 zones of Bogotá and Medellín, followed to relate the external exposome, above all particulate air pollution, to respiratory disease (ARI, asthma).

label: Butajira Nutrition, Mental Health, and Pregnancy Study
exposures: mycotoxin exposure | aflatoxin | maternal nutrition
quote: Butajira Nutrition, Mental Health, and Pregnancy (BUNMAP) Study, a population-based prospective cohort study aimed at evaluating the role of maternal nutrition, mycotoxin exposure, and mental health on prenatal and postnatal growth and development that was conducted between October 2017 and November 2020 in the Butajira Health and Demographic Surveillance Site under Addis Ababa University, Ethiopia.
note: Population-based pregnancy cohort in the Butajira HDSS designed to study maternal nutrition and mycotoxin (aflatoxin) exposure; outcomes are fetal and child growth, not a disease.

label: Primeiros Laços
quote: eighty low-income pregnant youth were randomized into two groups: intervention (HVP by nurses, n = 40) and control (healthcare as usual, n = 40).
note: Randomised trial of a nurse home-visiting programme for low-income pregnant adolescents and their children; the intervention is not an environmental exposure and pregnancy is not a disease.

label: Golestan Cohort Study
exposures: opium use | tobacco | alcohol use | tea drinking habits, including tea temperature | occupational history
quote: The primary aims of the GCS are: (i) To identify risk factors for OC by a comprehensive assessment of ethnicity, occupational history, socio-economic status, past medical history, family history of cancers, gastrointestinal symp- toms and signs, tobacco, opium and alcohol use, oral health, anthropometric characteristics, physi- cal activity and tea drinking habits, including tea temperature.
note: Population-based cohort in Golestan set up to study oesophageal cancer; its primary aim is to identify lifestyle risk factors (opium, tobacco, alcohol, hot tea, diet), in the manner of a diet/lifestyle-and-cancer cohort.

label: Norwegian Family Based Life Course Study
quote: All Norwegians participating in censuses from 1960 to 2001 were included.
note: Register-based cohort of the whole Norwegian census population for multigenerational life-course research; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: Chilean COVID-19 Biorepository
note: Nationwide Chilean biorepository of adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, for host-genetic studies of COVID-19 severity and long COVID; a patient cohort, not an exposure cohort.

label: Million Women Study
quote: The Million Women Study is a population-based cohort study of 1.3 million UK women.
note: Population-based cohort of UK women invited to breast screening, set up to study HRT and breast cancer; HRT is a medication, so not an environmental exposure cohort, but a population study of breast cancer.

label: Saudi Biobank
quote: This population included military service personnel and their families, members of the MNG-HA population (patients or healthy volunteers), health care workers, and students from the MNG-HA-related healthcare system.
note: National population biobank of Saudi nationals for research on common and rare diseases; environment is mentioned only in passing, so neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: Prospective Epidemiological Research Studies in Iran
quote: The PERSIAN project is an ongoing, nationwide, population-based prospective cohort that began enrolment in 2014 to characterise environmental, lifestyle, and genetic determinants of non-communicable diseases across Iran’s diverse populations.
note: Nationwide population-based Iranian cohort studying environmental, lifestyle and genetic determinants of non-communicable diseases in general; broad purpose, so no on both counts.

label: Generation Victoria
quote: All children living in Victoria, Australia, born between 4 October 2021 and 3 October 2023 and their parents/guardians are eligible for GenV’s ‘Cohort 2020s’.
note: Whole-population statewide birth and parent cohort in Victoria, a broad platform for child and adult health research; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: South Asia Biobank
quote: SAB is a cross-sectional population-based study that recruited participants from 118 surveillance sites that were centred on local primary community health care units in five study regions: Bangladesh, South India, North India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
note: Population-based biobank of South Asian adults for risk factors of diabetes, cardiovascular disease and other chronic diseases; the purpose is broad (chronic diseases) and environmental data are one of many measures.

label: Dementias Platform UK
note: Data platform pooling UK population and clinical cohorts (including Parkinson's and familial Alzheimer's cohorts) for dementia and neurodegeneration research; its stated purpose is dementia, with no exposure focus.

label: Iganga-Mayuge Health and Demographic Surveillance Site
quote: The IMHDSS cohort covers a catchment area of 155 km2 with a population of 95 000 individuals and is served by 23 health facilities.
note: Health and demographic surveillance of the whole population of an eastern Ugandan area, a general population-health platform; neither exposure- nor disease-defined.

label: HUNT4 70+
quote: All residents aged 70 and older in the catchment area received an invitation and an information letter about the HUNT4 study in general and the HUNT4 70+ study in particular.
note: Sub-study of HUNT4 inviting all residents aged 70+ for cognitive and health assessment, used for dementia and MCI prevalence and incidence; a population study of dementia, not an exposure cohort.

label: Coronagenes
note: Online volunteers sharing direct-to-consumer genotype data with COVID-19 questionnaires (cases and controls) to find genes for COVID-19 risk and severity; not selected by infection, so a population study of COVID-19; no environmental exposure.

label: German National Cohort
quote: Specifically, NAKO is designed to identify novel and better characterize established risk and protection factors for the development of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes, neurodegenerative and psychiatric diseases, musculoskeletal diseases, respiratory and infectious diseases in a random sample of the general population.
note: German national population cohort drawn at random from the general population with a broad purpose covering many chronic and infectious diseases; neither exposure- nor single-disease-focused.

label: The Malaysian Cohort
quote: TMC is a nationwide prospective cohort project, which recruited approximately 100 000 Malaysians aged between 35 and 70 y at baseline.
note: Nationwide Malaysian population cohort studying non-communicable diseases in general; broad purpose, no exposure focus.

label: Cancer Prevention Study-3
note: US adult cohort recruited by the American Cancer Society whose primary goal is cancer incidence and mortality, so a population study of cancer; lifestyle is studied but no exposure is a stated design focus.

label: Personalized Environment and Genes Study
exposure categories: chemical | metal | pesticide | occupational | radiation | diet | physical activity | built environment
exposures: environmental exposures | chemical and environmental exposures at work and home | pesticides and insecticides | chemical and metal exposures at work | ultraviolet light exposure | diet | physical activity | residential proximity to multi-pollutant point sources
quote: While most studies focus on a single disease or environmental exposure, PEGS collects data on multiple diseases and environmental exposures, including diet and lifestyle factors, in concert with genetic data.
note: NIEHS cohort (formerly the Environmental Polymorphisms Registry) built to collect exposome and genetic data on diverse North Carolina adults; exposure-centred design, but it covers many diseases rather than one.

label: Newfoundland and Labrador Genome Project
quote: The NL Genome Project was based on the random recruitment of participants from General Practice clinics from across the province that were 18 years of age and over, possessed a valid NL health card, and provided written consent.
note: General population genetics cohort of Newfoundland and Labrador recruited at random from GP clinics; no exposure or disease selection.

label: UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women's Cohort
quote: UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women’s Cohort (UKLWC) includes the 202,280 postmenopausal women from the general population who joined the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening and donated their samples and data for use in secondary studies
note: Bioresource of general-population postmenopausal women from an ovarian cancer screening trial, now an open platform for the study of common disease; participants were not selected for disease or risk, so no on both counts.

label: Kilifi Health and Demographic Surveillance System
note: Health and demographic surveillance population in Kilifi, Kenya, set up and used mainly to study the incidence and prevention of infectious diseases of childhood; no exposure focus.

label: Cancer Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort
exposures: diet and other lifestyle factors and exposures
quote: The Cancer Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort was established in 1992 and was designed to investigate the relation between diet and other lifestyle factors and exposures and the risk of cancer, mortality, and survival.
note: Diet-and-cancer subcohort of CPS-II, designed to relate diet and lifestyle exposures to cancer risk, like EPIC.

label: Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort
exposure categories: air pollution | chemical | water | diet | physical activity | built environment
exposures: early-life environmental exposures | air pollution | phthalates | drinking water source | chemicals | diet | physical activity
quote: The goal of the ECHO Program is to understand how the environment, from preconception through early childhood, influences child health and development to identify opportunities to mitigate the risk of disease and optimize health and thriving (4).
note: US consortium of pregnancy and paediatric cohorts built to study how early-life environmental exposures affect child health; its outcomes span several areas (perinatal, airway, obesity, neurodevelopment, positive health), so not a single-disease aggregation.

label: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study for the Next Generation
quote: The target population for the JPHC-NEXT is the total of 261,939 residents (130,602 men and 131,337 women) aged 40–74 years who were registered in the basic residence registers of the 16 municipalities at the time of enrollment in 2011–2016.
note: Japanese population-based cohort of municipal residents with the broad aim of risk factors for lifestyle-related disease and healthy life expectancy; neither exposure- nor single-disease-focused.

label: China Patient-centered Evaluative Assessment of Cardiac Events Million Persons Project
note: Nationwide Chinese population screening cohort run to identify people at high risk of cardiovascular disease, so a population study of cardiovascular disease; no exposure focus.

label: Africa Centre Demographic Information System
note: Open population surveillance cohort in rural KwaZulu-Natal set up to study the HIV epidemic (later extended to TB and NCDs); participants are all residents, not selected by exposure.

label: LifeGene
quote: The population-based LifeGene study (Sweden) randomly recruited individuals aged 18 to 43 years (n = 12 167).
note: Swedish population-based cohort recruited at random with a broad health purpose; no exposure or disease selection.

label: SG100K
note: Aggregation of four Singapore population cohorts whose stated focus is the determinants and prediction of cardiometabolic disease (cardiovascular disease and diabetes); no exposure focus.

label: South African Population Research Infrastructure Network
quote: Building on the strengths of three existing Health and Demographic Surveillance Systems, SAPRIN is a harmonized network of population-based cohorts with data that are made accessible for the research community and national policy makers.
note: National network of South African health and demographic surveillance populations with a general demographic and health purpose.

label: Lifecourse biological pathways underlying social differences in healthy aging
quote: Lifepath is a research consortium funded by the European Commission under Horizon 2020, designed to explore whether healthy aging is an achievable goal for the entire society.
note: Consortium of population cohorts studying how socioeconomic position affects healthy ageing; socio-economic status alone is not an environmental exposure and healthy ageing is not a disease.

label: Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention Programme
quote: a population-based cohort of more than 145 000 Austrian men and women followed for an average of nearly 10 years
note: Population risk-factor surveillance and prevention programme cohort in Vorarlberg covering cancer, cardiovascular disease and mortality broadly; no exposure or single-disease focus.

label: 45 and Up Study
quote: The Sax Institute's 45 and Up Study is a large-scale Australian cohort study of 267 151 men and women aged 45 years and over, randomly sampled from the general population of New South Wales (NSW), Australia.
note: Random sample of the NSW population aged 45+ as a resource for research on health and ageing; broad purpose.

label: International Health Cohorts Consortium
quote: IHCC membership criteria prioritize large population cohorts, capability for longitudinal health follow-up, broad participant selection, biological sample collection, and a commitment to data-sharing.
note: Consortium of large population cohorts and biobanks chosen for broad participant selection; collects general population cohorts, so no on both counts.
